verified_findings.title: REQ-D-004 / REQ-D-005 (demo seed RCDO shape + manager-with-5-8-reports narrative fixtures) have no architectural home

DATA_MODEL.md has NO seed table/migration; its only mention is 'Exact RCDO seed copy can be finalized during seed migration authoring' (open item). The shape IS locked elsewhere — DOMAIN_MODEL.md §'Seeded RCDO Shape' (1 Rally Cry / 3 DOs / 3 SOs each, 'locked decision') and DECISIONS.md 'Seed data' row ('1 manager, 5-8 reports, execution-SaaS RCDO; optional 2,000-record perf seed', Locked). verified_findings.finding: REQ-D-004 (seeded RCDO shape: 1 Rally Cry, 3 Defining Objectives, 3 Supporting Outcomes each) and REQ-D-005 (one manager with 5-8 direct reports plus plans, commitments, reviews, disputes, overdue states, carry-forward, and Graph failure states) are MVP requirements with hard acceptance signals. Finalizer must carry the locked seed decision into ARCHITECTURE.md so /tasks-gen produces a seed-migration task.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit demo-seed coverage to §6 (Physical Data Model) or §15 (Local/Test Runtime): a Flyway/seed migration creating the locked RCDO shape (REQ-D-004) and a deterministic demo fixture set (REQ-D-005) — 1 manager, 5-8 reports, plans across all lifecycle states, at least one overdue review, an open and a resolved dispute, a carry-forward chain, and a seeded FAILED outlook_calendar_sync_record — explicitly kept separate from the synthetic 2,000-record perf seed (REQ-D-008). Cite DOMAIN_MODEL 'Seeded RCDO Shape' and DECISIONS 'Seed data' as the locked source.

verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 representative endpoints include only 'POST /api/outlook-sync/{syncRecordId}/retry' — no GET to read an IC's own sync records. §9 RTK Query tag list includes 'sync records' but no route/view surfaces sync status (routes are /, /weekly-commit, /weekly-commit/history/:planId, /manager/command-center, /manager/heatmap). §12 step 8 asserts 'UI displays sync status and manual retry' but the read contract that delivers syncRecordId+FAILED state is unstated. PARTIAL not full gap: §7 says 'DTO fields should include IDs, display labels, state, timestamps, RCDO breadcrumbs, risk badges, and allowed actions' — a plausible carrier for sync status, and §7 also lists generic resource endpoints ('sync resources') implying a sync read may exist, but neither explicitly carries the owner's sync status/safeMessage. verified_findings.finding: REQ-I-005/REQ-UX-004/REQ-E-004 require failed sync state to be visible+recoverable to the affected IC, and §12 step 8 asserts the UI shows it, but no read contract delivers the syncRecordId/FAILED state: §7 exposes only the POST retry (though it mentions generic 'sync resources' and a flexible DTO), and §9 has a sync-record tag but no view surfaces it. Thin: plan DTOs could embed sync status, but the draft never says so.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7 state that the plan/commitment DTO (or a dedicated GET /api/outlook-sync?relatedId= read) returns current sync record status + safeMessage for the owning IC so the UI can render the warning and enable retry; in §9 attach the sync-status surface to the /weekly-commit IC workspace view.

verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed the draft itself is thin: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §3 lists the three review statuses ('NOT_REVIEWED, REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES, REVIEWED; overdue is derived') and §11 lists dispute-driven projection triggers, but neither states that REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES clears overdue while unresolved disputes keep the plan in risk filters. Unresolved disputes remain separate alignment risk.', locked decision) and DATA_MODEL.md manager_plan_summary carries both review_status and unresolved_dispute_count and is_review_overdue, plus the derived field rule 'isOverdue = now > review_due_at and status = NOT_REVIEWED' (so REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES is not overdue). EVALUATION_CRITERIA Demo Success Signals also encodes it. So the behavior is supported and locked but the binding draft doesn't state the rule — partial coverage; correctly proposed-edit.
verified_findings.finding: REQ-F-013's behavior (REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES satisfies the review SLA so it is not overdue, while unresolved disputes keep it in risk filters) is locked in DOMAIN_MODEL.md (lines 104-105) and structurally supported by DATA_MODEL (manager_plan_summary has review_status + unresolved_dispute_count + is_review_overdue, with isOverdue requiring status=NOT_REVIEWED). verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add to §11 (or §10 manager review service) one line: REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES satisfies the review SLA (is_review_overdue=false) while unresolved disputes continue to surface via unresolved_dispute_count/risk badges, anchoring REQ-F-013 in the binding doc.

verified_findings.title: Manager review-block Outlook sync trigger has no originating API action or job
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 line 301 lists the trigger as 'Manager review-block needed -> one manager review-block event per manager/week' with no defining condition. USER_FLOWS.md line 372 says 'Manager review-block event is needed: create or update manager calendar event with deep link to the command center' — also no originating action. The other two triggers ARE bound to explicit commands (lines 299-300: 'IC plan lock', 'IC starts reconciliation', which map to POST /lock and POST /start-reconciliation in §7 lines 158-159). §7 (lines 149-173) has no endpoint or job that emits MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK; §11 projection update triggers (lines 276-281) include 'Manager review status changes' but not review-block sync creation. REQ-I-001 and REQ-I-015 (REQUIREMENTS.md lines 49,63) require sync 'after ... manager review-block event creation' / 'one event per manager/week' without saying what creates it. DATA_MODEL.md line 250 defines event_kind MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK and line 248 related_type MANAGER_REVIEW, so the data home exists but the write path does not. The finding is accurate. Severity stays 'important' rather than lower: it is an in-scope MVP requirement (REQ-I-001/REQ-I-015) and the only sync trigger with no caller. However, note CONSTRAINTS.md line 203 and REQUIREMENTS.md line 200 explicitly designate this exact behavior as 'the first pressure-release candidate to simplify,' and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §20 line 489 lists 'review-block event automation' under 'Trim first' — so the gap is on a feature already flagged as droppable, which slightly tempers urgency.
verified_findings.finding: The Outlook sync flow lists three triggers, but the manager review-block event is the only one with no defined originating action. Lock and start-reconciliation map to explicit command endpoints; the review-block trigger is described only as 'needed' with no binding to an API call, lifecycle transition, or CronJob. §12 requires 'one event per manager/week' but nothing decides WHEN it fires or which transaction creates the sync record. The worker and sync-record creation for MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK have no caller.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12 (reflected in §7/§10/§11), define the concrete trigger: bind MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK sync-record creation to a specific event — recommend upsert in the manager review service (or plan-lock path) on the first direct-report plan lock of a given manager/week, idempotent on the existing unique sync key (owner_employee_id, related_type, related_id, event_kind). State which transaction owns the write. Explicitly document that because this is the designated first pressure-release candidate (CONSTRAINTS.md line 203, §20 line 489), trimming it degrades to no review-block event without affecting lock/review SLA — making the trigger spec light but unambiguous.

verified_findings.title: Single mark-reviewed endpoint does not specify REVIEWED vs REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES derivation or summary_note write
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 166 lists only 'POST /api/manager/reviews/{reviewId}/mark-reviewed' and §7 state constraints (lines 178-184) say only 'Manager review, dispute, and manager comment mutations require locked direct-report plans' — no status-derivation rule. DATA_MODEL.md line 176 constrains status to the three values, line 179 defines summary_note with no write path, and the manager_review derived field (line 189) only covers isOverdue. DOMAIN_MODEL.md lines 88-92 define three transitions (NOT_REVIEWED->REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES, NOT_REVIEWED->REVIEWED, REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES->REVIEWED) but the draft assigns none to an endpoint. USER_FLOWS.md lines 339-344 define the two-step distinction and line 343 ties REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES to 'one or more unresolved alignment disputes,' but no doc states the server-side derivation or whether resolving the last dispute auto-transitions to REVIEWED. The single endpoint cannot, as written, express the REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES->REVIEWED transition that DOMAIN_MODEL line 91 requires. Genuine underspecification of a load-bearing review contract.
verified_findings.finding: The manager review flow requires the status to resolve to REVIEWED or REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES (REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES = reviewed with >=1 unresolved dispute), but the draft never states how mark-reviewed chooses between them, where summary_note is written, or whether resolving the last open dispute auto-transitions REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES->REVIEWED and inside which endpoint.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7/§10, specify that mark-reviewed accepts an optional summary_note and derives status server-side from the current unresolved-dispute count for the plan's commitments (>0 -> REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES, else REVIEWED). State that POST /disputes/{id}/resolve re-evaluates the parent plan's review and may transition REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES -> REVIEWED when the last unresolved dispute closes. Both write summary_note/status inside the manager review service transaction and synchronously update manager_plan_summary.review_status / unresolved_dispute_count.

verified_findings.title: Recording reconciliation outcomes for commitments has no explicitly assigned API endpoint
verified_findings.verification_evidence: USER_FLOWS.md lines 199-207 require the IC to 'record outcomes for planned commitments' (step 4) and 'record outcomes for unplanned commitments' (step 7). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 156 lists 'PATCH /api/commitments/{commitmentId}' and §7 line 180 describes it only as 'rejects locked planned baseline field changes.' §7 line 182 says close-reconciliation 'requires reconciliation outcomes' — implying outcomes were written earlier — but no endpoint is named as the writer. The data home and mutability ARE specified: DATA_MODEL.md lines 147-149 define reconciliation_outcome, progress_status, outcome_note; DOMAIN_MODEL.md lines 188-193 list 'progress/status fields used during reconciliation', 'reconciliation outcome', 'outcome notes' as Mutable after lock. So PATCH /commitments/{id} is the obvious and only plausible home and the mutable-field set is contracted — the gap is that the draft never explicitly states PATCH is the outcome-recording path. Verdict is 'partial' (covered by an existing endpoint + mutable-field rules, but the write contract for the reconciliation half of PATCH is implicit) rather than a full confirmed_gap. The §16 test-list claim is accurate: lines 406-432 list lifecycle/SLA/baseline/disputes/sync/heatmap/auth but no outcome-recording write test.
verified_findings.finding: IC reconcile steps 4 and 7 require recording outcomes (reconciliation_outcome, progress_status, outcome_note), and close-reconciliation 'requires reconciliation outcomes,' but the draft never names the endpoint that writes them. PATCH /commitments/{id} is described only as the baseline-rejection endpoint; its role as the reconciliation-outcome write path is implicit, not stated.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7, explicitly state that PATCH /api/commitments/{id} is the contract for recording reconciliation outcome fields (reconciliation_outcome, progress_status, outcome_note) while the parent plan is in RECONCILING, accepting these mutable fields only in that state and rejecting baseline fields always after lock (it already enforces the latter). Add a matching integration test reference in §16 for the outcome-recording write path.

verified_findings.title: Organization timezone configuration has no persistent data home despite being load-bearing for week boundaries and SLA
verified_findings.verification_evidence: USER_FLOWS.md line 491 lists 'Organization configuration' as Data Touched and line 483 names the failure 'Due date cannot be calculated because organization timezone config is missing.' REQ-F-002 (REQUIREMENTS.md line 13) and REQ-O-003 (line 128) require org-timezone-based calculations. DATA_MODEL.md has NO organization/config table; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6 lists no such table and §14 (lines 356-375) covers region/domain/secrets but not org timezone. employee.timezone (DATA_MODEL.md line 34) is nullable and per REQ-X-008 user-local timezones are deferred. HOWEVER, the default behavior IS specified and contradicts the finding's premise that there is 'no source-of-truth to fail against': USER_FLOWS.md line 73 states 'For assessment/demo, the default organization timezone is America/Chicago unless the implementation environment overrides it,' REQ-F-002 line 13 says 'default America/Chicago for demo,' and CONSTRAINTS.md line 119 says 'Default assessment/demo timezone is America/Chicago.' So a default value and override mechanism exist conceptually; what is genuinely missing is the concrete config HOME (env var vs app property vs DB row) and reconciling the USER_FLOWS failure state with that default. Verdict 'partial': the value/default is covered, the persistent home and the fail-safe-vs-fail-hard reconciliation are not. The finding's own recommended fix (config property defaulting to America/Chicago, no org_config table) matches the corpus intent, so this is correctly scoped but slightly overstated as having 'no source-of-truth.'
verified_findings.finding: Org timezone is load-bearing for week boundaries, plan uniqueness, and reviewDueAt, and a USER_FLOWS failure state references missing org timezone config, but the draft never defines where the config lives (no organization_config table; §8/§14 do not state env var vs app property vs DB row). The default value (America/Chicago) is specified across docs, but the persistent home and the fail behavior are not pinned down.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §6/§14, state the source of truth for organization timezone — recommend an application config property defaulting to America/Chicago, supplied via Secrets Manager / Terraform variable in deploy (a full org_config table is overbuild for one week, since user-local weeks are deferred per REQ-X-008). Reconcile the USER_FLOWS.md line 483 failure state with the documented default: prefer fail-safe to the default America/Chicago rather than failing the calculation, and update the flow text accordingly.

verified_findings.title: Plan-shell generation idempotency has a data home but no test in the quality-gate list
verified_findings.verification_evidence: USER_FLOWS.md lines 40-49 define the success state 'Every active employee has at most one draft plan shell' and failure 'Duplicate plan conflict.' REQ-F-001 acceptance signal (REQUIREMENTS.md line 12): 'Rerunning generation for the same employee/week does not create duplicates.' ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §10 lines 263-266 states the DB unique constraint on employee/week 'provides final idempotency guard,' and §16 lines 406-432 list unit tests (lifecycle/SLA/baseline/disputes/sync state), integration tests (JPA/Flyway, authorization, projections, sync records), E2E (IC draft/lock/reconcile/carry-forward; manager review/dispute; heatmap; Outlook; auth denial), and perf — but NO generation-job idempotency / rerun-skip test. The data home (weekly_plan unique constraint, DATA_MODEL.md line 127) exists but no test asserts rerun behavior. Confirmed, and correctly scoped as nice-to-have for a one-week build since the DB constraint structurally prevents duplicates regardless of test presence.
verified_findings.finding: Shell generation idempotency (REQ-F-001 acceptance: rerun does not duplicate) is enforced by the weekly_plan unique constraint but has no test in §16's quality-gate list, which covers lifecycle/SLA/baseline/disputes/sync/heatmap/auth E2E but no generation-job test.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16, add a lightweight integration test for the generation job: rerunning generation for the same employee/week is a no-op (skips existing plans, no duplicate-key error surfaced as a failure), asserting the §10 'final idempotency guard' behaves as documented.

verified_findings.title: Carry-forward next-week shell + linked-commitment creation is a data write with no documented endpoint side-effect contract
verified_findings.verification_evidence: USER_FLOWS.md lines 204-207 require the backend to 'resolve the next Monday-Sunday week,' 'create the next-week draft plan shell if it does not already exist,' and 'create linked next-week draft commitments for carried-forward work'; lines 264-268 (Carry-Forward Target Decision) restate this as a locked decision and say the backend creates the missing shell then linked draft commitments. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 162 lists 'POST /api/commitments/{commitmentId}/carry-forward' but §7 state constraints (lines 178-184) say nothing about its cross-week writes. §11 line 281 DOES list 'Carry-forward creation' as a projection update trigger, and DATA_MODEL.md line 150 defines carry_forward_source_commitment_id, line 148 includes CARRIED_FORWARD as a reconciliation_outcome, and line 127 the unique (employee_id, week_start_date) constraint. So the data model, the decision, and the projection trigger ARE covered; what is missing is the explicit endpoint side-effect contract (multi-table transaction) and the idempotency interaction between carry-forward and the CronJob both creating the next-week shell on the shared unique key. Verdict 'partial': the behavior is described at the flow/decision level but not captured as an endpoint contract in §7/§10. Correctly nice-to-have for the timebox.
verified_findings.finding: Carry-forward (USER_FLOWS steps 9-11) requires resolving next week, creating the next-week DRAFT shell if missing, and creating linked DRAFT commitments, but §7 never states these multi-table side effects as the carry-forward endpoint's contract, nor how it races with the CronJob-generated next-week shell on the shared (employee_id, week_start_date) unique key.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7/§10, document the carry-forward endpoint side-effect contract: within one transaction, upsert the next-week DRAFT weekly_plan (idempotent on the employee/week unique key shared with the CronJob path) and insert a linked DRAFT weekly_commitment carrying carry_forward_source_commitment_id; set the source commitment's reconciliation_outcome to CARRIED_FORWARD. Explicitly note idempotency vs CronJob-generated shells (the unique constraint resolves the race; the loser no-ops).

verified_findings.title: progress_status field has no defined enum / check constraint
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED. DATA_MODEL.md:147 declares `progress_status varchar(32) null` with NO check clause, while every sibling status column carries one: state (118 `check (state in ('DRAFT','LOCKED','RECONCILING','RECONCILED'))`), commitment_kind (139), priority (143), work_type (144), confidence (145), alignment_status (146), reconciliation_outcome (148). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6:120 states the convention literally: 'VARCHAR status columns with check constraints' — progress_status violates it. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:190 lists 'progress/status fields used during reconciliation' as mutable-after-lock but never enumerates a value domain. PRD.md:259 lists 'Progress/status updates' as an allowed post-lock action but assigns no values. No state machine in DOMAIN_MODEL.md §67-143 references progress_status. The field is genuinely undefined and unconstrained. It is also functionally redundant with reconciliation_outcome (148), which already carries the COMPLETED/PARTIALLY_COMPLETED/BLOCKED/CANCELED state during reconciliation — the only lifecycle phase progress_status could matter in.
verified_findings.finding: progress_status is the only status-type column in the schema with no enumerated value set and no CHECK constraint, contradicting the stated physical convention (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6:120). Its value domain, its relationship to reconciliation_outcome, and whether it gates anything are unspecified everywhere. It is functionally redundant with reconciliation_outcome for the only phase it could be used in.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §6, drop progress_status entirely (recommended for the one-week build — reconciliation_outcome + outcome_note already cover reconciliation progress) OR, if retained, give it an explicit CHECK enum (e.g. NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/DONE), document its relationship to reconciliation_outcome, and state it is nullable-until-reconciliation and NOT part of the locked baseline. Add a §16 test note.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §6 (Physical Data Model: weekly_commitment.progress_status); cross-ref §5 mutable-after-lock list

verified_findings.title: Single reconciliation_outcome enum cannot represent partially-completed AND carried-forward simultaneously
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED that the collision exists and is unaddressed. DATA_MODEL.md:148 is a single-valued enum with all five values in one column. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:138 'Carry-forward is an outcome on the source commitment and creates a linked draft commitment in the next weekly plan.' PRD.md:249 'Carry-forward is not a terminal state for the original commitment. It is an outcome that creates a linked commitment in the next weekly plan.' USER_FLOWS.md steps 4 and 8 (lines 199,204) have the IC 'record outcomes for planned commitments' AND separately 'select carry-forward where appropriate' — never stating these occupy the same single field or are mutually exclusive. No artifact resolves whether a partially-completed-and-carried item is representable. The gap is real. NOTE: the architecture is internally consistent in treating these as one outcome set (DOMAIN_MODEL.md:128-138, REQ-F-027), so this is a scoping ambiguity to resolve, not a contradiction.
verified_findings.finding: reconciliation_outcome is single-valued, so a commitment that is partially completed AND has remaining work carried forward cannot be modeled — the IC must drop either the partial-completion fact or the carry-forward link. PRD.md:249 frames carry-forward as orthogonal to completeness (a non-terminal outcome spawning a linked commitment), which the single enum cannot capture. No artifact acknowledges or resolves the collision.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Decide in finalized §5/§6: (a) keep the single enum and explicitly state CARRIED_FORWARD is mutually exclusive with completion outcomes (partial+carry NOT representable) as a deliberate, tested MVP simplification — recommended for one week; or (b) split into completion_outcome + a nullable carry_forward producing carry_forward_source_commitment_id. State the chosen rule as a locked limitation with a §16 test.

verified_findings.title: Reconciliation-close completeness rule does not require an outcome on every commitment
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7:182 'POST /close-reconciliation requires RECONCILING, reconciliation outcomes, and Supporting Outcome links for all unplanned commitments' — 'reconciliation outcomes' is plural/unscoped and never says every planned commitment must have a non-null outcome. DATA_MODEL.md:148 makes reconciliation_outcome nullable. USER_FLOWS.md:217 'Require outcomes for commitments included in reconciliation' is ambiguous ('included in' could read as opt-in), and :235 lists 'Required outcomes are missing' without defining 'required.' REQ-F-029 (REQUIREMENTS.md:40) 'close only when required outcomes and links are complete' — 'required' is never pinned. The whole point of the locked baseline (PRD.md:52 'planned-vs-actual reconciliation is meaningful', REQ-E-005) is defeated if a plan can reconcile with NULL planned outcomes. Genuine gap.
verified_findings.finding: The close-reconciliation precondition never states that EVERY planned commitment must carry a non-null reconciliation_outcome before close; reconciliation_outcome is nullable, so a plan could reach RECONCILED with planned commitments silently un-outcomed, breaking planned-vs-actual truth. 'Required'/'included in reconciliation' is never defined.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §7, make close-reconciliation require: state=RECONCILING AND every PLANNED commitment has non-null reconciliation_outcome AND every UNPLANNED commitment has both a non-null reconciliation_outcome and a supporting_outcome_id. Add the invariant to §5 and a §16 unit test ('close rejected when any planned commitment has NULL outcome').

verified_findings.title: Plan state machine documents only forward preconditions, not rejection of illegal/backward/self transitions
verified_findings.verification_evidence: PARTIAL. The negative behavior IS partly covered in the flow artifacts: USER_FLOWS.md:157 lists 'Plan is already locked, reconciling, or reconciled' as a lock failure state and :233 lists 'IC attempts to reconcile a draft or already reconciled plan' as a reconcile failure state; REQ-T-001 (REQUIREMENTS.md:147) acceptance signal is 'Invalid transitions fail.' So the requirement to reject illegal transitions is captured. What is genuinely missing is only the API-contract binding: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7:179-182 lists positive source-state preconditions but does not bind the rejection to the problem-details state-conflict response shape it defines at §7:147, nor enumerate self-loops/backward edges. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:80 says 'No unlock/amend flow exists in MVP' but gives no rejected-transition table. So the gap is a documentation-precision gap, not an unspecified behavior — appropriately nice-to-have, and the claim that the requirement is missing is slightly overstated since USER_FLOWS+REQ-T-001 already mandate it.
verified_findings.finding: The rejection of illegal/backward/self transitions is mandated by USER_FLOWS.md:157,:233 and REQ-T-001, but the §7 API contract does not bind these to a concrete state-conflict (409 + problem-details) response, and no canonical legal-edge table exists. This is a precision gap for a build whose correctness rests on the FSM.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §7, add: lifecycle command endpoints reject any call whose plan is not in the exact required source state with the problem-details state-conflict response (constraint name + safe message + trace id, per §7's stated error shape). Optionally add a 4-edge transition table to §5 stating all other edges (including self-loops/backward) return 409. Reference REQ-T-001.

verified_findings.title: Overdue derivation predicate stated two different ways across artifacts
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED divergence. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:97 'OVERDUE when now > reviewDueAt and status is NOT_REVIEWED' and :106 same; DATA_MODEL.md:189 'isOverdue = now > review_due_at and status = NOT_REVIEWED' — both use the equality form. But USER_FLOWS.md:464 'isOverdue is true when current time is past reviewDueAt and review status is not REVIEWED or REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES' — the complement form. REQ-F-012 (REQUIREMENTS.md:23) sides with the equality form ('review status is NOT_REVIEWED'). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §3:47 only says 'overdue is derived.' With the locked 3-value enum (DATA_MODEL.md:176) the two formulas are logically identical TODAY, so this is correctly a low-severity wording-consistency item, not a live bug — exactly as the finding scopes it.
verified_findings.finding: The overdue predicate is written two ways: equality-on-NOT_REVIEWED (DOMAIN_MODEL.md:97,:106; DATA_MODEL.md:189; REQ-F-012) vs the complement 'not REVIEWED or REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES' (USER_FLOWS.md:464). Identical under today's 3-value enum, but the finalized doc should carry one canonical formula so a future status value cannot make them diverge.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §5 (and §11 where is_review_overdue is materialized), state ONE canonical predicate: `is_review_overdue = (now > review_due_at) AND status = 'NOT_REVIEWED'`, and note manager_plan_summary.is_review_overdue copies it. Reference REQ-F-012/REQ-T-004.

verified_findings.title: Manager-review record lifecycle on a not-yet-locked plan is unspecified; no review state before lock
verified_findings.verification_evidence: PARTIAL. The storage handling IS present: manager_review.weekly_plan_id is UNIQUE (DATA_MODEL.md:174), its status enum has no pre-lock value (:176), manager_plan_summary.review_status is nullable (:284), USER_FLOWS.md:460 'creates or updates the Manager Review record when the plan locks' and :148 success-state 'Manager review state is NOT_REVIEWED' confirm the row appears at lock. REQ-F-003 (REQUIREMENTS.md:14) requires managers to distinguish not-started/draft/locked plans, and manager_plan_summary.plan_state (DATA_MODEL.md:283) carries that distinction independent of review_status. So the data model CAN represent the pre-lock state (review_status NULL, plan_state DRAFT/empty). What is genuinely missing is only the explicit prose rule that review_status=NULL is the canonical pre-lock representation and that is_review_overdue must stay false while NULL — a small determinism note for risk-badge derivation, not a structural gap. Hence nice-to-have/partial, not important.
verified_findings.finding: The schema can represent a pre-lock plan (manager_review row absent, review_status NULL, plan_state from manager_plan_summary), but no artifact states that review_status=NULL is the canonical 'no review yet / not locked' representation or that is_review_overdue must remain false while review_status is NULL. This leaves heatmap/summary risk-badge derivation for DRAFT/NOT_STARTED plans slightly underdetermined.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §11 (and §5) state: a manager_review row exists only for LOCKED+ plans; for DRAFT/NOT_STARTED plans manager_plan_summary.review_status is NULL and renders as 'No review yet (not locked)' with no overdue badge; is_review_overdue stays false while review_status is NULL. Tie to REQ-F-003.

verified_findings.title: One-open-dispute partial unique index predicate should be carried verbatim into finalized §6
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED as correct-but-underspecified-at-the-draft-summary-level. DATA_MODEL.md:209 already states the full predicate: 'partial unique index allowing at most one unresolved dispute per commitment where status in OPEN,IC_RESPONDED'. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:38 agrees 'at most one open or IC-responded unresolved dispute at once', and REQ-F-018 (REQUIREMENTS.md:29) + REQ-T-005 (:151) lock the behavior. The only thinness is ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6:133 which summarizes it as 'unresolved dispute partial unique index by commitment' WITHOUT the IN ('OPEN','IC_RESPONDED') predicate. So the rule is fully specified in DATA_MODEL.md; the finalized ARCHITECTURE.md just needs to copy the predicate so an implementer reading only §6 does not index status='OPEN' alone. Correctly a proposed-edit. (Minor citation note: the finding cites §6:135; the actual line is §6:133.)
verified_findings.finding: The one-unresolved-dispute rule is correctly and fully modeled in DATA_MODEL.md:209 (partial unique index over status IN ('OPEN','IC_RESPONDED')). The only gap is that ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6:133 summarizes it without the predicate, risking an implementer indexing status='OPEN' only and wrongly allowing a second dispute while one is IC_RESPONDED.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §6 write the index explicitly: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON alignment_dispute(commitment_id) WHERE status IN ('OPEN','IC_RESPONDED')`. Add a §16 test note that opening a second dispute while one is IC_RESPONDED is rejected (not only while OPEN). Per REQ-F-018/REQ-T-005.

verified_findings.title: Locked-baseline immutable field list differs across DOMAIN_MODEL and DATA_MODEL; alignment_status mutability is the load-bearing nuance
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED that the lists differ and that the alignment_status nuance is real and load-bearing — upgrading severity rationale. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:177-187 immutable list (title, description, Supporting Outcome link, priority, work type, confidence, planned/unplanned marker, source plan/week) and :188-195 mutable list explicitly including 'manager-owned alignment status and manager note' and 'dispute-related fields.' DATA_MODEL.md:165 baseline rule lists 'title, description, supporting outcome, priority, work type, confidence, commitment kind, plan/week ownership' and is SILENT on alignment_status. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §5:107 'Locked planned fields cannot change' and §7:180 'PATCH /commitments rejects locked planned baseline field changes' name NO carve-out. The dispute flow REQUIRES alignment_status to mutate post-lock: USER_FLOWS.md:287 manager flags 'Misaligned', and DATA_MODEL.md:146 makes alignment_status a non-null commitment column — so if an implementer reads §7:180 + DATA_MODEL.md:165 and freezes all non-listed commitment fields, the dispute-driven alignment transition breaks. This is a genuine contradiction risk for the dispute lifecycle, so 'important' is justified, but it is verdict=partial because DOMAIN_MODEL.md:194 already classifies alignment_status as mutable — the resolution exists in one artifact and just needs to be made authoritative and tied to the PATCH rejection set.
verified_findings.finding: The immutable-after-lock field lists are not identical: DATA_MODEL.md:165 omits alignment_status entirely while DOMAIN_MODEL.md:194 explicitly classifies manager-owned alignment_status (and manager_note, dispute fields) as MUTABLE post-lock. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §5:107/§7:180 say only 'locked planned fields cannot change' with no carve-out. alignment_status is a non-null commitment column (DATA_MODEL.md:146) that the dispute flow MUST mutate post-lock (USER_FLOWS.md:287). An implementer freezing all non-listed commitment fields would break the dispute lifecycle.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In finalized §5/§7 enumerate the exact immutable-after-lock set (the 8 IC-owned planned fields) AND the explicit post-lock-mutable exceptions: reconciliation_outcome, outcome_note, progress_status (if kept), alignment_status + manager_note (manager-owned), and alignment_dispute record fields. Bind PATCH /commitments rejection to precisely the immutable set so manager/dispute-driven alignment_status transitions are not accidentally blocked. Reference REQ-F-008/REQ-T-003.

verified_findings.title: No system/service principal authorization path for CronJob plan generation and sync worker
verified_findings.verification_evidence: The draft's authorization model is exclusively human-principal: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §8 says 'Service methods check owner/self access and manager direct-report access before repository mutation/read' and lists only IC/Manager denial cases; REQ-S-011 says 'Service-layer checks enforce self/direct-report access for reads and mutations.' Two non-user actors exist with no self/direct-report relationship: (a) the CronJob — USER_FLOWS.md 'Scheduled Weekly Plan Shell Generation' Actor is 'EKS Kubernetes CronJob / plan generation service' creating plans 'For each employee' (step 4), and §10 'EKS CronJob invokes generation job/API'; (b) the sync worker — ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 steps 5-7 and USER_FLOWS.md Outlook flow steps 5-8 have the worker load the sync record and write graph_event_id/status back. Nothing in §8, §10, §12, THREAT_MODEL, or DECISIONS defines a SYSTEM principal, a system-context entrypoint, or an explicit exemption from self/direct-report checks for these actors. The nullable audit_event.actor_employee_id (DATA_MODEL.md) is the only hint of system actors, with no principal model behind it. This is a genuine, uncovered architectural gap. NOTE: the worker is a SEPARATE Spring Boot deployable (§4 wc-sync-worker, ADR-009 separate images) that talks to its own repositories, not through wc-api's authorization service — so for the worker specifically the 'must bypass authz service' framing is partly moot; the real undefined item is the CronJob's path into wc-api domain services and the actor identity on system-written audit rows. Severity lowered from critical to important: for a one-week build this is a documentation/wiring clarification, not a missing capability — the implementer can run the CronJob/worker outside the request-scoped authorizer, and there is no evidence the authorizer would hard-block them. It is still a real gap because leaving it unspecified invites either an impossible mandatory-authz reading or an undocumented, untested bypass.
verified_findings.finding: The authorization architecture (§8, REQ-S-011) is defined only for human IC/Manager principals doing self/direct-report-scoped reads and mutations, but two production actors carry no user principal: the EKS CronJob that creates weekly_plan shells for every active employee, and the wc-sync-worker that writes graph_event_id/status back to outlook_calendar_sync_record rows. No artifact defines how these system actors authenticate to or are exempted from the self/direct-report authorization service, nor what actor identity their audit_event rows carry (the column is nullable but the principal model is unspecified).
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §8 define a third SYSTEM/service principal alongside IC/Manager. Specify: (a) the CronJob enters wc-api plan generation through a dedicated system-context entrypoint (not the JWT/demo-header request filter) and is explicitly exempt from self/direct-report checks because it carries no user request; (b) the wc-sync-worker is a separate deployable operating on its own repositories under a SYSTEM context, permitted to transition sync-record state and write graph_event_id but not to touch commitment/review/dispute content; (c) system mutations still write audit_event with a SYSTEM marker (resolving the nullable actor_employee_id). One short paragraph in §8 plus a note in §10/§12 closes it.

verified_findings.title: Multiple managers per direct report vs. single manager_employee_id on review/dispute is unresolved
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed schema-vs-model tension. DATA_MODEL.md manager_relationship has unique '(manager_employee_id, direct_report_employee_id)' plus index '(direct_report_employee_id, active)' — this permits N active managers for one report, and there is NO partial-unique constraint on direct_report_employee_id. Meanwhile manager_review.weekly_plan_id is 'not null unique' with a single manager_employee_id (one review row per plan), and alignment_dispute carries a single manager_employee_id. No artifact declares single-active-manager as an invariant: PRD.md invariants say only 'A manager can only access direct reports' and 'A manager cannot access another manager's direct report by manipulating IDs' (access scope, not cardinality); REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-F-017 says 'Only the direct manager can explicitly resolve' (singular phrasing, not an exclusion of multi-manager); ASM-009/DECISIONS seed is '1 manager, 5-8 reports' (a demo seed shape, explicitly 'Smaller demo seed if needed' as fallback — not a locked schema invariant). DOMAIN_MODEL.md 'Employee may manage many direct reports' addresses the manager side, never the report side. So the single-row review/dispute model silently assumes one manager per report while the schema allows several, and authorization ('direct-report access' is binary) would pass for both. Genuine gap.
verified_findings.finding: The schema permits a direct report to have more than one active manager (manager_relationship is unique on the pair and indexed by direct_report alone, with no single-manager constraint), but manager_review is one UNIQUE row per plan with a single manager_employee_id and alignment_dispute carries a single manager. No artifact resolves which manager owns the review/dispute when a report has two managers, whether both may act, or how the single-row model and binary 'direct-report access' check stay consistent.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: For the one-week build, take option (a): declare single-active-manager-per-report as a locked MVP invariant in §5/§6/§8 and back it with a partial unique index on manager_relationship(direct_report_employee_id) WHERE active = true, so the single-row manager_review/alignment_dispute model and the binary direct-report authorization check are provably consistent. If multi-manager is ever wanted, that is deferred work requiring arbitration rules; do not leave it implicit.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §8 Authorization (primary); §5 Domain model; §6 Physical data model

verified_findings.title: Comment write authorization and targetId IDOR resolution asserted as 'inherits target visibility' but not made actionable
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Partially covered. The cross-team denial IS in the threat model: THREAT_MODEL.md Security Tests lists 'Manager cannot read/mutate non-direct-report plans, reviews, disputes, comments, or heatmap cells' — comments are explicitly named. REQ-F-014 grants 'Manager can comment on direct-report locked plans/commitments' and §7 state constraints say 'Manager review, dispute, and manager comment mutations require locked direct-report plans' — so the locked-plan precondition for MANAGER comments IS stated. What is genuinely under-specified: (1) §13 and DATA_MODEL.md comment rules say authorization 'inherits target visibility' / 'follows the target resource's visibility rules' — this is a READ-visibility rule, and the write-eligibility derivation (resolve target_type+target_id back to the owning weekly_plan: commitment->plan, review->plan, dispute->commitment->plan) is never spelled out; (2) POST /api/comments takes targetType/targetId from the client (§7) — a classic IDOR surface — and no artifact states the service must resolve+authorize the target before insert (it is implied by the threat-model test but not specified as behavior); (3) §8's 'Required denial cases' list omits comments entirely (it has IC/Manager plan, dispute, heatmap, demo-header cases but no comment case); (4) whether an IC may comment on a MANAGER_REVIEW or ALIGNMENT_DISPUTE row is undefined (PRD only grants ICs 'respond to disputes'). So the intent is covered by the threat-model test and REQ-F-014, but the resolution chain, the parent_comment_id cross-target check, and the §8 denial case are missing — partial, not a clean confirmed gap.
verified_findings.finding: Comment write authorization is asserted as 'inherits target visibility' (§13, DATA_MODEL) but not made actionable: the service must resolve client-supplied target_type+target_id back to the owning weekly_plan and authorize before insert (POST /api/comments is an IDOR surface), reject parent_comment_id belonging to a different target, and define whether an IC may comment on review/dispute rows. The manager-locked-plan precondition (REQ-F-014, §7) and cross-team comment denial (THREAT_MODEL test) are covered, but the target-resolution chain and a §8 comment denial case are missing.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §13/§7 state the comment authorizer must resolve target_type+target_id to the owning plan (commitment->plan, review->plan, dispute->commitment->plan), reject unseeable/nonexistent targets (closing targetId IDOR), apply role+state rules (IC may comment on own plan/commitment/dispute; manager only on direct-report targets when plan is LOCKED-or-later per REQ-F-014), and reject a parent_comment_id from a different target. Add a comment denial case to §8's 'Required denial cases' to mirror the existing THREAT_MODEL comment test.

verified_findings.title: Per-id ownership scoping for heatmap drill-down cell and sync-record retry not stated as denial cases
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Split verdict. The heatmap-cell IDOR is partly covered: THREAT_MODEL.md Security Tests explicitly lists 'Manager cannot read/mutate non-direct-report plans, reviews, disputes, comments, or heatmap cells' — cells named — and manager_heatmap_cell carries manager_employee_id (DATA_MODEL.md), so the check is trivially available. What is under-specified: §8's authorization text 'Projection endpoints scope by manager's direct-report relationship before returning rows' is phrased for multi-row LIST returns, and §7 'command-center and heatmap endpoints return only direct reports' is also list-level; the SINGLE-resource read GET /api/manager/heatmap/{cellId}/drilldown (§7) is not called out as needing a per-row manager_employee_id check, and §8 'Required denial cases' lists 'IC accesses team heatmap' but not 'manager opens another manager's drill-down cell.' The sync-record retry IDOR is genuinely uncovered: POST /api/outlook-sync/{syncRecordId}/retry (§7) operates on a record owned by owner_employee_id (DATA_MODEL.md), and NO artifact — not §8 denial cases, not THREAT_MODEL tests (which never mention sync-record authorization beyond duplicate-event idempotency) — states retry must verify the caller owns (IC) or manages (manager) that owner. So: heatmap cell = partial (threat-test exists, §8 denial-case + per-id wording missing); sync retry = confirmed gap. Net: partial.
verified_findings.finding: Single-resource projection reads/mutations by id lack explicit per-row ownership checks. In §7/§11 state single-resource projection reads authorize on the row's own manager_employee_id (not just list filtering) and the retry handler resolves owner_employee_id and applies self/direct-report. Add the sync-retry scoping to the THREAT_MODEL security-test list, where it is currently absent.

verified_findings.title: Dispute respond/resolve ownership-derivation chain not spelled out
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Largely covered at the architecture level. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §8 'Required denial cases' explicitly lists 'Manager opens/resolves dispute for non-direct report' and 'IC resolves a dispute' — both endpoints' core denial cases are named. §7 state constraints add 'dispute ... mutations require locked direct-report plans.' THREAT_MODEL.md adds 'Manager cannot read/mutate non-direct-report ... disputes' and STRIDE Elevation-of-Privilege 'IC resolves manager dispute ... Mitigation: service-level authorization checks.' REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-F-016/017 and USER_FLOWS.md failure state 'IC attempts to resolve a dispute directly' reinforce it. DATA_MODEL.md provides the derivation data (alignment_dispute.commitment_id -> commitment.weekly_plan_id -> plan.employee_id). What the finding flags as missing — the literal walk 'respond authorizes off plan.employee_id; resolve authorizes off CURRENT manager_relationship not the stored opener' — is a true implementation-precision nuance, but it is the kind of detail the named denial cases plus the centralized domain authorization service (REQ-S-011) already imply, and REQ-T-007 already mandates integration tests for direct-report authorization/IDOR denial. verified_findings.finding: The dispute respond/resolve endpoints' authorization is already covered by §8's named denial cases ('Manager opens/resolves dispute for non-direct report', 'IC resolves a dispute'), §7 state constraints, the THREAT_MODEL tests, and REQ-T-007's IDOR integration-test mandate. The only residual nuance — that resolve should authorize against the CURRENT manager_relationship rather than the stored dispute.manager_employee_id, and respond against plan.employee_id derived via commitment->plan — is an implementation-precision note, not a missing architectural decision.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Optional: add one clarifying sentence to §8 that dispute authorization derives ownership via commitment->plan->employee_id and evaluates the manager check against the current active manager_relationship, not the stored dispute opener. verified_findings.title: Manager read-only vs IC read-write boundary on plan/commitment content not encoded as an explicit matrix
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Partially covered by intent, not by an explicit authorization-mode statement. The substantive control IS asserted: PRD.md 'Managers cannot silently rewrite an IC's Supporting Outcome link in MVP' and USER_FLOWS.md failure state 'Manager attempts to change the IC's Supporting Outcome link without IC revision'; REQ-F-009 (manager inspects draft details for direct reports only) and REQ-F-010 (manager flag/review against draft rejected); DECISIONS 'Manager visibility: Direct-report only; can view drafts, formal review after lock.' §7 state constraints gate the lock-stage for manager review/dispute/comment. What is genuinely absent: §8 expresses authorization only as self vs direct-report (a binary predicate) and never states that 'direct-report access' is READ-ONLY for managers across all plan/commitment baseline content in every state, while managers may WRITE only manager_review/alignment_dispute/(post-lock) comment artifacts. An implementer wiring the central authorizer could grant a manager the same write predicate as the owner for direct-report plans, since both satisfy the single 'direct-report access' gate. The finding is real but lower severity: multiple other artifacts encode the no-rewrite intent, so this is a clarity/defense-in-depth hardening, not an undefended hole. Partial.
verified_findings.finding: §8 expresses authorization as a binary self/direct-report predicate and never states the read-vs-write asymmetry per role: managers have READ-only access to direct-report plan/commitment baseline content in every state and may WRITE only manager_review/alignment_dispute/(post-lock) comment artifacts. The no-silent-rewrite intent is covered elsewhere (PRD, USER_FLOWS failure state, REQ-F-009/010), but an implementer using only §8's single direct-report predicate could grant a manager owner-equivalent write capability.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §8 state the role/operation matrix explicitly: managers = READ-only on direct-report plan/commitment content in all states + WRITE only on review/dispute/post-lock-comment artifacts; ICs = read+write on own plan/commitment content (subject to lifecycle/baseline rules) but no review/dispute resolution writes. Reference the matrix from §10 so each service knows its allowed actor-operation pairs. Low effort, hardens an intent already stated in PRD/USER_FLOWS.

verified_findings.title: Carry-forward self-scope across two plans and same-owner target constraint not explicitly confirmed
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Real but minor, and largely safe by construction. USER_FLOWS.md IC Reconciles steps 9-11 and REQ-F-028 confirm the backend creates the next-week shell if missing and inserts linked draft commitments — an IC writing into a DIFFERENT weekly_plan than the source. Both plans belong to the same IC, so §8's self-access check passes by construction, and DATA_MODEL.md weekly_plan unique '(employee_id, week_start_date)' gives idempotent shell creation (REQ-F-001/REQ-D-002). What is not explicitly stated anywhere: that the carry-forward/reconciliation service authorizes against the SOURCE plan's employee_id AND constrains the created/target next-week plan to that same employee (preventing carrying work into another employee's plan). This is a thin, easily-satisfied invariant rather than an open hole — the unique constraint and self-check already make the dangerous case (cross-employee carry) hard to reach, and there is no endpoint that lets the IC name an arbitrary target plan (carry-forward is keyed off commitmentId, §7). It also intersects system-principal (the same shell-creation path the CronJob uses). Partial: worth a one-line confirmation, not a structural fix.
verified_findings.finding: Carry-forward and reconciliation have the IC write into a second weekly_plan (the next-week shell). Because both plans share the same employee_id the self-access check passes by construction and the (employee_id, week_start_date) unique constraint makes shell creation idempotent, but no artifact explicitly states the service authorizes against the source plan's employee_id and constrains the target next-week plan to that same owner. This is a thin invariant to confirm, not an exposed hole (carry-forward is keyed off commitmentId, not a client-named target plan).
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add one sentence to §8/§10: carry-forward and reconciliation authorize against the source plan's employee_id (self-access) and any next-week plan they create or target must be owned by that same employee, relying on weekly_plan(employee_id, week_start_date) unique for idempotent shell creation. Note this is the IC-triggered counterpart to the CronJob shell-creation path (ties to the system-principal finding).

verified_findings.title: Standalone manager-owned `managerNote` chess-layer field has no column anywhere
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed gap. PRD.md:129 lists `managerNote: optional, manager-owned` as a distinct chess-layer field alongside priority/workType/confidence/alignmentStatus. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:194 explicitly lists 'manager-owned alignment status and manager note' under 'Mutable after lock' — i.e. a note that lives ON the commitment, not on a dispute. DOMAIN_MODEL.md:209 glossary: 'Chess layer: strategic metadata on commitments: priority, work type, confidence, alignment status, manager note.' REQ-F-006 acceptance signal (REQUIREMENTS.md:17): 'Priority, work type, confidence, alignment status, and manager-owned note model are represented.' But DATA_MODEL.md weekly_commitment columns (lines 137-151) have NO manager_note/alignment_note column. The only manager_note in the entire schema is alignment_dispute.manager_note (DATA_MODEL.md:202) which is `text not null` and bound to a formal OPEN->IC_RESPONDED->RESOLVED state machine — a different concept than an optional, lightweight, commitment-level note. So a manager-owned chess-layer note has no home, and the chess-layer/REQ-F-006 requirement is unsatisfiable as schematized.
verified_findings.finding: The chess-layer `managerNote` (optional, manager-owned, on the commitment) named in PRD, DOMAIN_MODEL glossary, and DOMAIN_MODEL's mutable-after-lock list has no column in weekly_commitment. The only manager_note is the REQUIRED alignment_dispute.manager_note tied to a formal dispute. There is no place for a lightweight optional manager alignment note distinct from a dispute, yet REQ-F-006's acceptance signal requires the manager-owned note model to be represented.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §6 (and bake into DATA_MODEL.md weekly_commitment) pick and document one source of truth: (a) declare 'manager note = alignment_dispute.manager_note; no standalone commitment note exists' and reframe DOMAIN_MODEL.md:194/209 + PRD's chess-layer `managerNote` so the implementer does not add a phantom column; OR (b) add a nullable `manager_alignment_note text null` (manager-owned, mutable-after-lock, audit-logged per REQ-S-006) to weekly_commitment. Given REQ-F-006 lists it as commitment chess metadata alongside alignment_status, (b) is the cleaner match. Either way state it explicitly so the field is not silently dropped. Severity is important, not critical: it is a one-column or one-sentence resolution with no security/correctness blast radius for the one-week build.

verified_findings.title: `progress_status varchar(32)` has no check constraint and no enumerated value set
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. DATA_MODEL.md:147 `progress_status varchar(32) null` carries no check constraint. Every other status column does: weekly_plan.state (118), commitment_kind (139), priority (143), work_type (144), confidence (145), alignment_status (146), reconciliation_outcome (148), manager_review.status (176), alignment_dispute.status (200)/flag_type (201), sync record related_type/event_kind/status (248/250/251), comment.target_type (220). DATA_MODEL.md:13 Physical Model Defaults: 'Status fields: VARCHAR with check constraints, not native Postgres enums' — and REQ-D-010 (REQUIREMENTS.md:78) makes it binding: 'Lifecycle/status fields use VARCHAR values with check constraints.' progress_status's allowed values are never enumerated anywhere (DOMAIN_MODEL.md:190 only says 'progress/status fields used during reconciliation'). So it is the single status column violating the model's own convention, with an undefined value set, and potentially redundant with reconciliation_outcome (148).
verified_findings.finding: progress_status is the only status-style column in the schema without a check constraint and without an enumerated value set, violating DATA_MODEL's own convention and REQ-D-010. Its overlap with reconciliation_outcome is undefined, making Flyway DDL and the REQ-T-002/T-003 unit tests non-deterministic.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §6 either (a) define the value set and add `check (progress_status in (...))` (e.g. NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/AT_RISK/DONE), or (b) if it is redundant with reconciliation_outcome, drop it and state reconciliation_outcome is the single progress field. Pick one so the migration and tests are deterministic. Important (not nice-to-have) because it is an explicit convention/requirement violation that touches the test acceptance signals, but it is a small bounded fix.

verified_findings.title: `alignment_status` ownership contradiction and its relationship to `alignment_dispute.flag_type` / projection counts is unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed contradiction. PRD.md:128 and REQ-F-006 (REQUIREMENTS.md:17) present alignmentStatus as IC-assigned chess metadata ('IC can assign chess-layer metadata ... alignment status'). But DOMAIN_MODEL.md:194 lists 'manager-owned alignment status' as Mutable after lock. The same column (DATA_MODEL.md:146, ALIGNED/NEEDS_REVIEW/MISALIGNED) is thus described as both IC-owned-at-draft and manager-owned-after-lock with no handoff rule. Separately, alignment_dispute.flag_type (DATA_MODEL.md:201, NEEDS_REVISION/MISALIGNED) overlaps the alignment_status vocabulary (NEEDS_REVIEW vs NEEDS_REVISION; MISALIGNED in both) and the model never states whether opening/resolving a dispute writes back to weekly_commitment.alignment_status. The projection counts manager_plan_summary.needs_review_count/misaligned_count (DATA_MODEL.md:289-290) and manager_heatmap_cell.needs_review_count/misaligned_count (316-317) have no documented source field — USER_FLOWS.md:563 only says 'Risk badges must derive from commitment/review/dispute/reconciliation state' without pinning which.
verified_findings.finding: alignment_status has a genuine ownership contradiction (IC-set per PRD/REQ-F-006 vs manager-owned-after-lock per DOMAIN_MODEL:194) with no documented handoff, and its relationship to alignment_dispute.flag_type is unspecified, leaving the projection misaligned_count/needs_review_count derivation non-deterministic.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §6/§11 document (1) who writes alignment_status in DRAFT vs after LOCK — recommend IC sets it as self-assessment at draft, then it is read-only on the commitment after lock and manager concerns flow only through alignment_dispute; and (2) the exact projection derivation, e.g. misaligned_count = commitments with alignment_status=MISALIGNED OR an open dispute with flag_type=MISALIGNED. Important because the contradiction is real and it directly determines projection count correctness (the core manager-value surface).

verified_findings.title: Per-manager/week MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK sync record cannot key cleanly into outlook_calendar_sync_record
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. REQ-I-015 (REQUIREMENTS.md:63) and its acceptance signal lock 'one event per manager/week ... rather than creating per-report events'; DECISIONS.md:54 and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md:301 say the same. But outlook_calendar_sync_record is uniquely keyed (owner_employee_id, related_type, related_id, event_kind) with related_id `not null` and related_type in {WEEKLY_PLAN, MANAGER_REVIEW} (DATA_MODEL.md:248-249, 264), and event_kind includes MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK (250). manager_review is unique per weekly_plan_id (DATA_MODEL.md:174) — i.e. per direct-report-plan, not per manager/week. There is no per-manager/week entity to point related_id at, so a MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK record would have to point at one arbitrary report's manager_review.id; when a second report locks, a different manager_review.id yields a different related_id and the unique index permits a duplicate review-block record, contradicting one-per-manager/week. Idempotency therefore cannot hold at the DB level as schematized.
verified_findings.finding: The documented one-MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK-event-per-manager/week idempotency cannot be enforced by the outlook_calendar_sync_record unique key because there is no per-manager/week related entity — related_id (NOT NULL) can only point at a per-plan manager_review row, so each newly locked report produces a new key and a duplicate review-block sync record.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §6/§12 define MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK keying explicitly. Options: add a related_type value (e.g. MANAGER_WEEK) with a deterministic per-manager/week related_id, OR make related_id nullable for review-block and add `period_week_start date null` so the unique constraint for that case is (owner_employee_id, event_kind, period_week_start). State the exact composite-key strategy so idempotency holds at the DB level, not just in app logic. Important: review-block automation is on the documented trim list (DRAFT §20, RISKS Trim Order #1), so if trimmed this is moot — but if built as specified the schema cannot enforce the stated invariant.

verified_findings.title: `risk_badges text[]` has no enumerated badge vocabulary or check
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed at the stated low severity. DATA_MODEL.md:321 `risk_badges text[] not null default '{}'` has no constraint (a Postgres text[] cannot carry a simple value check). A candidate badge set exists but is not pinned in DATA_MODEL: REQ-F-021 (REQUIREMENTS.md:32) 'misaligned, needs-review, blocked, carry-forward, unreviewed, or overdue review' and USER_FLOWS.md:567 repeats the same list as a 'locked decision'. Tests assert badges match seeded data: REQ-T-008 (REQUIREMENTS.md:154) 'Counts/risk badges match seeded data' and REQ-E-003 (171). With the vocabulary unpinned in the data model, writer/reader/test drift is possible.
verified_findings.finding: risk_badges has no pinned closed vocabulary in DATA_MODEL; the candidate list lives only in REQ-F-021 and USER_FLOWS:567 as prose, so the projection writer, frontend, and seeded-data tests could drift on exact badge strings.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §11 (and as a note on DATA_MODEL risk_badges) pin the closed badge enum (e.g. MISALIGNED, NEEDS_REVIEW, BLOCKED, CARRY_FORWARD, UNREVIEWED, REVIEW_OVERDUE), enforced in the projection-writer service and shared as a TS union on the frontend. Cheap to specify; keeps writer/reader/tests in sync. Nice-to-have is the correct severity for a one-week build.

verified_findings.title: No @Version / optimistic locking — double-lock and projection-update races unguarded
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Partially covered, and overstated at 'important' for this build. The mechanism gap is real: no @Version/optimistic/pessimistic locking appears in DATA_MODEL.md, DOMAIN_MODEL.md, or ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md — weekly_plan.state (DATA_MODEL.md:118) is the only guard and lifecycle transitions are read-then-write in service methods (DRAFT §10:258-260). Synchronous projection updates do happen inside the same service transaction across many trigger points (DATA_MODEL.md:353-354), a genuine concurrent-write surface. HOWEVER the SYMPTOM is already acknowledged: RISK-003 (RISKS.md:14) 'Projection table drift makes manager dashboard inaccurate' (High) and RISK-014 (RISKS.md:25) 'heatmap read model hides wrong risk badges' (High) both carry mitigations (synchronous updates + rebuild job/CLI + projection tests). What is missing is the concurrency MECHANISM, not awareness of the failure mode. For a single-tenant, seeded-persona, one-week demo (REQ-D-005: 1 manager + 5-8 reports), concurrent double-lock of the same plan by one IC is low-likelihood, so this is nice-to-have, not important.
verified_findings.finding: There is no documented concurrency-control mechanism (@Version or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) for lifecycle state transitions and synchronous projection updates; only weekly_plan.state read-then-write guards them. The drift symptom is covered by RISK-003/RISK-014 mitigations, but the mechanism that would actually prevent lost-update/double-transition races is unspecified.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a one-line decision to §6/§10: a `version bigint` (@Version) column on weekly_plan (and optionally weekly_commitment, manager_review, and projection rows) so JPA optimistic locking rejects concurrent transitions with 409, OR document that lifecycle command services re-assert the precondition state inside the transaction and lock the weekly_plan row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) when mutating it plus its projections. Cheap to state; closes the gap behind RISK-003/014. Nice-to-have for a single-tenant one-week demo.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §6 Physical Data Model (version column) + §10 Backend Service Architecture (lifecycle transaction concurrency)

verified_findings.title: Index coverage is broadly adequate for 200ms / 2000 rows; minor drilldown/filter paths uncovered
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Already covered for the stated targets; the finding rebuts itself. The manager read load (REQ-NF-001 <200ms, REQ-D-008 2,000-record views, REQ-NF-003 indexed heatmap aggregation) is carried by the indexed projection tables: manager_plan_summary unique (manager,employee,week) + index (manager,week,plan_state) + (manager,review_status) (DATA_MODEL.md:298-300); manager_heatmap_cell unique grain + (manager,week) + (manager,defining_objective) (326-328); weekly_plan unique (employee_id,week_start_date) (127) covers IC current-plan retrieval. ADR-006 (DECISIONS.md:141-160) and §19 chose read-model tables precisely to satisfy dashboard speed without N+1. The finding itself concludes the proposed extra indexes (priority/work_type composites) are 'gold-plating / overbuild for one week' and that filter scans are bounded by projection scoping — so there is no actionable gap, only an optional documentation note.
verified_findings.finding: Index coverage already meets the 200ms/2000-row targets through the indexed projection tables (per ADR-006). The only residual items — a (weekly_plan_id, supporting_outcome_id) composite for drilldown and per-attribute filter indexes — are explicitly overbuild for a 2,000-row, projection-scoped dataset, by the finding's own conclusion.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Optional only: add a one-line note in §6 that projection tables carry the manager read load and that dashboard priority/work_type/alignment_status filters operate on already-narrowed (one manager, one week) projection-scoped row sets, so no per-attribute index set is warranted. No new index is required for the MVP target.

verified_findings.title: employee.role is single-valued (IC|MANAGER) but a manager who is also an IC is a real shape
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Partially covered. DATA_MODEL.md:32 `role varchar(50) not null check (role in ('IC','MANAGER'))` is single-valued. verified_findings.finding: The and/or (plan-owning + report-managing) capability is documented (DOMAIN_MODEL:12, 31-32) and authorization derives from manager_relationship not role, so the substance is covered. verified_findings.title: No endpoint to set per-commitment reconciliation outcomes; PATCH /commitments mutability split is unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 156 lists `PATCH /api/commitments/{commitmentId}` and line 180 describes it ONLY as '`PATCH /commitments/{id}` rejects locked planned baseline field changes' — it never states the endpoint accepts the mutable reconciliation set. close-reconciliation (line 182) 'requires `RECONCILING`, reconciliation outcomes, and Supporting Outcome links' yet no endpoint is documented to WRITE reconciliation_outcome / outcome_note / progress_status. The mutable-after-lock set is real: DOMAIN_MODEL.md lines 188-193 list 'progress/status fields used during reconciliation / reconciliation outcome / outcome notes / carry-forward link' as Mutable after lock (the finding mis-cited this to DATA_MODEL.md lines 188-193, but DATA_MODEL.md line 148-149 does define reconciliation_outcome/outcome_note columns). REQ-F-027 requires outcome values 'persisted and displayed'; USER_FLOWS.md lines 200/203/207 require the IC to record outcomes. So the write path genuinely has no documented contract. Downgraded from critical to important because the carrier endpoint (PATCH) and the field set both already exist in the corpus — this is an unstated contract, not a missing capability, and is trivially closeable in finalization for a one-week build.
verified_findings.finding: §7 documents PATCH /api/commitments/{id} solely as the reject-locked-baseline endpoint and never states it (or any endpoint) accepts the mutable reconciliation fields {reconciliation_outcome, outcome_note, progress_status}. close-reconciliation depends on outcomes existing but no endpoint is specified to persist them. verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7 state that during RECONCILING `PATCH /api/commitments/{commitmentId}` accepts the mutable set {reconciliation_outcome, outcome_note, progress_status} (plus supporting_outcome_id for unplanned commitments) while still rejecting any immutable planned-baseline field change, and add the precondition that outcome writes require parent plan state = RECONCILING. List the immutable vs mutable field sets inline (they already exist in DOMAIN_MODEL.md §Locked Baseline Representation) so the contract is unambiguous.

verified_findings.title: Only mark-reviewed endpoint exists; REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES transition has no defined trigger
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 166 exposes only `POST /api/manager/reviews/{reviewId}/mark-reviewed`. DOMAIN_MODEL.md lines 88-91 define three source transitions (NOT_REVIEWED -> REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES, NOT_REVIEWED -> REVIEWED, REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES -> REVIEWED) but no doc states WHICH endpoint produces REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES or back to REVIEWED. §11 line 280 lists 'Manager review status changes' as a projection trigger without naming the owning command. The SLA hinge is real and covered semantically — USER_FLOWS.md line 464 ('isOverdue true when ... status is not REVIEWED or REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES') and lines 343-352 confirm REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES satisfies SLA, and REQ-F-013 — but the *computation rule* (does mark-reviewed inspect open disputes? does opening/resolving a dispute flip an already-reviewed plan?) is genuinely unspecified. Downgraded from critical to important: REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES is plausibly derivable at read time from review-marked + unresolved-dispute-count (manager_plan_summary already stores unresolved_dispute_count, DATA_MODEL.md line 293), so the gap is an unstated derivation/transition rule rather than a missing capability — but it must be pinned because the two-status distinction is stored, not purely derived (manager_review.status check at DATA_MODEL.md line 176 includes REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES).
verified_findings.finding: Of the two terminal review statuses, only the path to REVIEWED has an endpoint. How a review reaches REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES — and how it transitions back to REVIEWED when the last dispute resolves — is undefined: it is unclear whether mark-reviewed computes the status from open disputes at mark time, or whether opening/resolving a dispute mutates an already-marked review. §11's 'Manager review status changes' projection trigger has no owning endpoint.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7 state that mark-reviewed computes the resulting status server-side (REVIEWED when the plan has zero unresolved disputes for that manager at mark time, else REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES), that opening a dispute on an already-reviewed plan transitions REVIEWED -> REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES, and resolving the last unresolved dispute transitions REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES -> REVIEWED. verified_findings.title: §9 never defines how the remote obtains the Auth0 token/identity from the PA host in REMOTE mode
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §9 (lines 210-238) covers only React/Vite/RTK Query, routes, shared singletons (line 219: 'Shared singleton dependencies: React, React DOM, Redux Toolkit, React Redux'), Module Federation 'exposing one route/module entry and remoteEntry.js' (line 218), and the persona switcher — zero text on host->remote token acquisition. §8 (lines 188-208) is backend-only: line 190 'Real mode: Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server validates Auth0 JWT issuer/audience' describes the API VALIDATING a JWT, never the frontend PRODUCING one. CONSTRAINTS.md line 90 confirms 'WC does not duplicate PA-owned global routing, Auth0/session context...' and REQ-I-008 (REQUIREMENTS.md line 56) restates it, so WC cannot run its own login — the token MUST come from the host, yet no host accessor/shared-singleton-auth contract exists anywhere. ADR-004 (DECISIONS.md lines 109-123) and REQ-I-013 (line 61) define only 'remote name, remoteEntry.js, one exposed route/module entry point, and shared React/React DOM/Redux dependencies' and stop at 'Exact PM remote parity remains a verification item.' Corpus-wide grep for getAccessToken/prepareHeaders/host token/token accessor returned nothing. This is a genuine, load-bearing gap for the production-shaped micro-frontend claim (§1 line 13).
verified_findings.finding: In REMOTE (PA-hosted) mode, §9 mandates 'RTK Query for all API calls' but never specifies how WC's baseQuery obtains an authenticated identity. WC does not own the Auth0 login flow (CONSTRAINTS line 90; REQ-I-008), so its baseQuery cannot run its own OAuth2/PKCE — it must receive a bearer token or a token-getter from the host. No artifact documents a host->remote identity contract (no shared-singleton auth module, no injected getAccessToken() accessor, no bootstrap input). Without it, tasks-gen must invent the single most load-bearing runtime seam, and the 'production-shaped remote' claim is unsubstantiated for auth.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §9 add a 'Host integration contract' subsection: in REMOTE mode the PA host passes an auth accessor into the exposed module entry — either a getAccessToken(): Promise<string> callback prop on the mounted root, or a shared singleton auth module the host populates. RTK Query prepareHeaders calls that accessor to set Authorization: Bearer <jwt>. In STANDALONE mode the same accessor is satisfied by the demo identity provider. Record this as an explicit extension of the ADR-004 remote contract (keep OQ-004 flagged for exact PM parity) so the seam is stubbable now.

verified_findings.title: baseQuery has no documented rule for choosing demo header vs Authorization: Bearer JWT
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §9 line 237 ('Persona switcher sends demo identity header to API') and §8 lines 190-192 (real mode = Auth0 JWT; 'Demo mode: backend accepts demo identity header only when DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED=true') describe two header strategies but never connect them in the frontend baseQuery. THREAT_MODEL.md line 13 names the boundary with header 'X-Demo-Employee-Id' and STRIDE 'Production backdoor' / line 73 'demo auth remains enabled in production' but covers only BACKEND rejection (REQ-S-008, line 95). No artifact defines a client-side auth-mode flag or the prepareHeaders branch that selects header-vs-bearer. Corpus grep for VITE_/prepareHeaders/baseQuery returned nothing. Confirmed gap. Severity downgraded from critical to important: the backend already enforces the mutually-exclusive gate (DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED, REQ-S-008) so a wrong client choice fails safe (rejected requests) rather than silently shipping the backdoor; the missing piece is the deterministic frontend selection rule, which is real but a tier below the host-token gap because it cannot itself produce the production-backdoor outcome the backend already blocks.
verified_findings.finding: §9/§8 define both a demo-identity-header path and an Auth0-JWT path but never tell the frontend baseQuery which to attach at request time. The two are mutually exclusive on the backend (REQ-S-008 / THREAT_MODEL line 13), so the frontend needs a single explicit mode signal driving prepareHeaders to attach EITHER X-Demo-Employee-Id OR Authorization: Bearer, never both. That decision is unspecified, leaving tasks-gen to invent it and risking a demo header configured into the production remote build.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §9 specify one frontend auth-mode source of truth (e.g. VITE_AUTH_MODE = demo | auth0, default demo for standalone, auth0 when hosted). prepareHeaders branches on it: demo attaches X-Demo-Employee-Id: <selectedPersona>; auth0 attaches Authorization: Bearer <token from the §9 host accessor>. State the two are never combined and the demo branch is configured/compiled off in the production remote build, mirroring the backend DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED gate.

verified_findings.title: No CORS contract between wc.<domain> (frontend) and api.wc.<domain> (API)
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 lines 366-367 define Frontend 'wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}' and API 'api.wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}' as separate origins; CONSTRAINTS.md lines 158-159 and DECISIONS.md lines 21-22 (ADR-001/010) lock this split. verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §9 line 218 names only 'Module Federation remote exposing one route/module entry and remoteEntry.js' and lines 222-228 list four routes; it never names the exposed module artifact or assigns providers (BrowserRouter/Redux store/identity provider/persona switcher) to a standalone wrapper vs the shared module. verified_findings.title: Lazy-loaded routes are required (REQ-NF-005) but §9 only lists routes without a code-splitting strategy
