verified_findings.title: "One review-block event per manager/week" has no enforceable key in the sync-record table
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED CONTRADICTION. DATA_MODEL.md L248 `related_type varchar(32) not null check (related_type in ('WEEKLY_PLAN','MANAGER_REVIEW'))` and L264 unique `(owner_employee_id, related_type, related_id, event_kind)`. Both allowed related_types are per-IC-per-week grains; there is NO `week_start_date` column on `outlook_calendar_sync_record` (L246-260 lists none) and NO per-manager-per-week related grain. grep confirms `MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK` exists ONLY as an `event_kind` value (DATA_MODEL.md L250), never as a related_type, and no `MANAGER_REVIEW_WEEK`/`review_week` token exists anywhere in the corpus. Meanwhile the 'one per manager/week' intent is asserted in 4 places: REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-I-015 L63, DECISIONS.md L54 ('One manager review-block event per manager/week' Locked), CONSTRAINTS.md L219 ('MVP uses one manager review-block event per manager/week'), ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 L301. The unique key genuinely cannot express the manager+week grain, so the locked decision is unimplementable as the schema stands. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from critical to important: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §20 L489 lists 'review-block event automation' as the FIRST trim candidate, and REQUIREMENTS.md L200 names 'automatic Outlook manager review-block event creation' as 'the first candidate to simplify' — so this is the most-disposable feature in a one-week build, not a core-correctness blocker.
verified_findings.finding: The locked decision 'one manager review-block event per manager/week' (REQ-I-015, DECISIONS L54, CONSTRAINTS L219, §12 L301) cannot be expressed by the sync-record uniqueness `(owner_employee_id, related_type, related_id, event_kind)`. related_type is restricted to WEEKLY_PLAN/MANAGER_REVIEW (both per-IC-per-week), there is no week_start_date column, and no per-manager-per-week related grain. A manager with 5-8 reports locking their plans in one week will produce either N distinct MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK rows (calendar spam, the exact thing forbidden) or silent collisions, depending on what related_id the implementer picks. Real gap, but for the single most-disposable feature in the build.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12 + §6 define an explicit per-manager-per-week grain for MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK. Add a `week_start_date date` column to `outlook_calendar_sync_record` and either (a) add related_type value 'MANAGER_REVIEW_WEEK' with related_id = a deterministic manager+week key, OR (b) make the review-block uniqueness `(owner_employee_id, event_kind, week_start_date)` with owner = the manager. State the first review-block trigger of the week creates the row and every later direct-report lock is an idempotent upsert against it. Because this rides the first-to-trim feature, an acceptable cheaper resolution is to explicitly mark review-block sync as deferred/stretch and remove MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK from the MVP event_kind enum until the grain is added.

verified_findings.title: Whose calendar the manager review-block targets, and during whose transaction it fires, is unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 L301 only says 'Manager review-block needed -> one manager review-block event per manager/week'; USER_FLOWS.md L372 says 'create or update manager calendar event with deep link to the command center' but never names the owner. DATA_MODEL.md L247 `owner_employee_id uuid not null references employee(id)` carries NO statement that for MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK it must be the manager. The trigger is a direct report's lock (USER_FLOWS.md L274 'Trigger: A direct report locks a weekly plan'), an IC-context transaction, so an implementer could plausibly set owner = the locking IC. THREAT_MODEL.md L18 ('Sync Worker -> Microsoft Graph') and the trust-boundary table cover token/scope but never which calendar a review-block writes to. grep for 'owner.*manager' found no binding statement. Genuine specification hole. Note this is tightly coupled to finding #1 and shares the same trim-first review-block feature, so it is important rather than critical.
verified_findings.finding: The review-block event must land on the MANAGER's calendar, but its trigger is a direct report's plan lock (IC-context transaction). The draft never states owner_employee_id = the manager for MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK, nor whether the row is created inside the IC's lock transaction (actor = IC) or by a separate manager-scoped step. An implementer can set owner = locking IC, putting the block on the wrong calendar and worsening the one-per-manager dedup problem.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12 state explicitly: for MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK, owner_employee_id = the direct manager of the locking IC, resolved via manager_relationship; the row is upserted within the lock transaction but keyed to manager+week (per finding #1); the Graph adapter writes to that manager's calendar. Add manager-resolution to the §10 'Outlook sync record service' responsibilities.

verified_findings.title: Draft never states whether there is ONE SNS topic + ONE SQS queue or many; routing/filtering left to implementer
verified_findings.verification_evidence: PARTIALLY COVERED. Cardinality IS consistently implied as one-of-each: DECISIONS.md L24 'SNS lifecycle fanout, SQS sync queue, separate EKS worker, DLQ' (all singular), ADR-003 L98-99 'publishes lifecycle events to SNS; SQS subscription delivers jobs to a separate EKS sync worker' (singular), DIAGRAM_PLAN.md L42-44 / L53 draws exactly one SNS box, one SQS box, one DLQ with `API --> SNS --> SQS --> Worker`. grep confirms NO 'filter policy', 'message attribute', or per-eventKind topic/queue language anywhere — so per-kind fan-out is plainly not intended. The genuinely-missing piece is narrower than claimed: not the topology (which is unambiguously single-of-each by the diagram + singular decisions), but the explicit statement that the worker DISPATCHES on eventKind. §12 L324-325 carries `eventKind` in the payload and Graph adapter modes (L332-336) branch on real/demo, but no line says the worker routes IC_PLANNING/IC_RECONCILIATION/MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK to different handlers. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from important to nice-to-have: the Terraform-topology risk the finding raises is already resolved by the consistent singular decisions + the diagram, so the only real residual is documenting worker dispatch.
verified_findings.finding: The SNS/SQS cardinality is implied as one topic + one queue by DECISIONS L24, ADR-003, and DIAGRAM_PLAN (single boxes), so the Terraform-topology ambiguity the finding fears is largely already settled. What is genuinely undocumented is the worker's dispatch-by-eventKind: the payload carries eventKind (§12 L325) but no line states the worker routes the three event kinds to different builders/handlers.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12 add one binding sentence: ONE SNS topic ('wc-lifecycle') with ONE SQS subscription/queue ('wc-outlook-sync') feeding the worker; the worker dispatches on the eventKind field (IC_PLANNING / IC_RECONCILIATION / MANAGER_REVIEW_BLOCK) to the matching Graph payload builder; SNS subscription filter policy is unused in MVP. Reference this single-topology in §14 Terraform scope.

verified_findings.title: Manual retry 'republishes/requeues' is never disambiguated to SNS-publish vs direct SQS-send, and worker-side dedup on redelivery is unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: MIXED. Part A (republish vs requeue) is a CONFIRMED GAP: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 L343 'republishes/requeues from the same sync record', REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-I-010 L58 'republishes or requeues', USERS.md L76 'republishes or requeues', USER_FLOWS.md L389 'republish/requeue' — all four use the same ambiguous either/or and grep confirms NO sendMessage-vs-Publish / direct-SQS distinction anywhere. Since §12 L302-303 routes the normal path API->SNS->SQS, whether retry re-enters at SNS or jumps to SQS is genuinely undefined. Part B (at-least-once redelivery dedup) is PARTIALLY COVERED, not absent: THREAT_MODEL.md L17 ('SQS -> Sync Worker ... Main Risks: Duplicate processing, replay ... MVP Mitigation: Graph event IDs, sync state machine, DLQ') and L39 ('worker loads current authoritative state from DB'), plus §12 L341-342 (load authoritative payload from PostgreSQL, reuse graphEventId to update not create) and DOMAIN_MODEL.md L161 ('Graph retry must reuse an existing sync record to avoid duplicate events') collectively address duplicate-Graph-event prevention. What is NOT stated is the explicit guard for two SQS deliveries of the same syncRecordId while status=SYNCING (the concurrent-skip rule). So the duplicate-EVENT outcome is covered; the concurrent-redelivery state guard is the residual gap.
verified_findings.finding: Manual retry's 'republish or requeue' is genuinely ambiguous across all four artifacts — re-publishing to SNS (full fan-out) and directly sending to SQS behave differently and have different idempotency implications, and the corpus never picks one. Separately, while duplicate Graph EVENTS are prevented (graphEventId reuse + load-from-DB + state machine, per THREAT_MODEL L17/39, §12 L341-342, DOMAIN_MODEL L161), the specific worker rule for handling two at-least-once SQS deliveries of the same syncRecordId concurrently (e.g. while status=SYNCING) is not stated.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12 pick one retry path: retry sets FAILED->RETRY_REQUESTED and the API re-publishes the same pointer to the SNS topic (keeps one publish path), then worker transitions RETRY_REQUESTED->QUEUED->SYNCING. Add the explicit redelivery guard: on receiving a syncRecordId the worker loads the row and, if status is SYNCED or actively SYNCING, treats it as a no-op; it only (re)attempts Graph when status in {QUEUED, RETRY_REQUESTED}, reusing graphEventId to update rather than create.

verified_findings.title: Sync-record state machine lists 6 states but no transition table, transition owners, or DLQ-terminal handling
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §12 L304-310 enumerates the six states (PENDING_PUBLISH, QUEUED, SYNCING, SYNCED, FAILED, RETRY_REQUESTED) and L312-321 gives a numbered flow narrative, but NO line assigns each transition to an owner (API after publish vs worker on receive vs worker on Graph response). DATA_MODEL.md L251 has the status check constraint and L258 `retry_count integer not null default 0` with NO max-attempt threshold anywhere (grep for max-attempt found nothing tied to retry_count). The DLQ-terminal question is genuinely unanswered: RESEARCH.md R-005 L124 notes 'SQS DLQs are configured through redrive policy and maxReceiveCount' but the draft never connects maxReceiveCount to a sync-row terminal state; DOMAIN_MODEL.md L162 says 'Repeated Outlook worker failures can route messages to SQS DLQ, but user-facing retry remains sync-record based' — confirming DLQ is message-level only and leaving the row's terminal state undefined. DIAGRAM_PLAN.md Diagram 6 (L200-218) shows Success/Failure/Retry/DLQ boxes but no per-state owner and no terminal-after-DLQ state. For a record that drives the UI warning/retry affordance (REQ-I-005 L53), the missing transition table is a real implementation hole. 'important' is the correct severity.
verified_findings.finding: §12 lists 6 sync states but provides no transition table, no per-transition owner (API vs worker vs Graph-response), and no defined terminal state after retries exhaust and the message lands in the DLQ. retry_count exists with no max threshold; DLQ is purely message-level, so the sync row can sit in SYNCING/FAILED indefinitely with no 'dead' terminal. Since this record drives the user-visible warning/retry UI, the ambiguity directly affects what the IC/manager sees.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a transition table in §12: API writes PENDING_PUBLISH in the core txn; after SNS publish API sets QUEUED; worker on receive sets SYNCING; Graph success -> SYNCED (+graphEventId); Graph failure -> FAILED (+failure_code, safe_message, retry_count++). Manual retry FAILED->RETRY_REQUESTED->(republish)->QUEUED. State that DLQ landing is message-level only and the sync row remains FAILED (the user-visible retryable terminal); note retry_count is informational and SQS maxReceiveCount governs DLQ independently.

verified_findings.title: Worker has no configured frontend base URL to build deep links, and standalone vs PA-host deep-link target is unaddressed
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED. REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-I-003 L51 'Outlook events include lifecycle context and deep links to the relevant WC plan or manager command center' (PRD explicit) and PRD.md L195 'Include lifecycle context and deep links to the weekly plan or manager command center' both REQUIRE deep links. The pointer-only payload correctly excludes the URL (§12 L323-330; REQ-I-014 L62), so the WORKER must build the link from its own config. But grep for ROOT_DOMAIN shows it appears ONLY as frontend/API domain config (REQ-O-008, DIAGRAM_PLAN L22/35/37, ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 L365-367, DECISIONS L51/L229, CONSTRAINTS L158-160) — NEVER as worker deep-link config. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 L375 only says 'Worker and CronJob use Secrets Manager-injected config' with no WC_FRONTEND_BASE_URL / ROOT_DOMAIN passthrough. CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.md L101 lists 'deep links' as an integration deliverable. Separately, DIAGRAM_PLAN.md Diagram 8 (L238-249) establishes WC runs both standalone AND as a PA Module-Federation remote, yet nothing states whether deep links target the standalone wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} origin or a PA-host route — leaving the most user-visible Graph payload field undefined. Confirmed gap, important.
verified_findings.finding: Deep links into the WC plan / manager command center are PRD-required (PRD L195, REQ-I-003) and must be built by the worker because the queue payload is pointer-only. But §14 only says the worker uses Secrets-Manager config and never injects a frontend base URL / ROOT_DOMAIN into the worker (grep confirms ROOT_DOMAIN is only ever frontend/API config). And because WC runs both standalone and as a PA Module-Federation remote (DIAGRAM_PLAN Diagram 8), the draft never says whether deep links point at the standalone WC origin or a PA-host route.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12/§14 give the worker an explicit WC_FRONTEND_BASE_URL (= https://wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} for the assessment) injected via Secrets Manager / config, and define deep-link patterns: IC events -> {base}/weekly-commit (or /weekly-commit/history/{planId}); review-block -> {base}/manager/command-center. State the standalone/MVP decision that deep links use the WC origin, and note the production hook where PA may rewrite to a host-shell route.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §12 Outlook Sync (Deep links) and §14 AWS Deployment (worker config)

verified_findings.title: DLQ is attached only to SQS (worker failures); SNS delivery-failure DLQ is researched but not decided
verified_findings.verification_evidence: VERIFIED but minor. RESEARCH.md R-005 L126 explicitly states both options: 'SNS subscriptions can use SQS DLQs for failed deliveries; an SQS queue DLQ is appropriate for worker processing failures.' Every downstream artifact attaches a DLQ only to the SQS queue: DECISIONS.md L24 / ADR-003 L99 ('SQS DLQ captures repeated worker failures'), CONSTRAINTS.md L145 ('SQS dead-letter queue is included for Outlook sync jobs'), ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 L371 (SQS/DLQ) and §12, DIAGRAM_PLAN.md L44/L53 (single 'SQS DLQ' box). No SNS-delivery-failure DLQ decision exists anywhere. The finding is accurate, and its own severity (nice-to-have) is correct: for a single in-account SNS->SQS subscription this is genuinely low risk, and the research line even pre-justifies the SQS-DLQ choice as 'appropriate for worker processing failures', so it is close to already-reasoned. Just needs the deliberate choice written down so the Terraform author does not silently leave SNS delivery failures undetected.
verified_findings.finding: RESEARCH.md R-005 notes both an SNS DLQ (failed SNS->SQS delivery) and an SQS DLQ (worker processing failures) are available, but every downstream artifact attaches a DLQ only to the SQS queue. For a single in-account SNS->SQS subscription this is low risk, but the deliberate choice is never stated, so a finalizer/Terraform author could leave SNS delivery failures undetected without realizing it was an intentional MVP scope cut.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14 add one line: MVP attaches a DLQ to the SQS queue (redrive policy, maxReceiveCount) for worker processing failures; SNS->SQS delivery failures rely on SNS retry within the same account, and a dedicated SNS DLQ is out of MVP scope (noted as a production-hardening item).

verified_findings.title: No workload owns Flyway migration execution — API and worker will race on RDS
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed across all artifacts. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4 lines 61-62 define wc-api and wc-sync-worker as separate Spring Boot apps, both on the same RDS; §10 line 265 makes the CronJob a third Spring Boot 'generation job/API'. CONSTRAINTS.md line 34 ('Flyway migrations.') and DATA_MODEL.md line 11 ('Migration tool: Flyway.') only name the tool, never a runner. THREAT_MODEL.md line 15 ('WC API -> PostgreSQL/RDS ... Spring services, JPA, Flyway') implies the API runs it but the worker and CronJob are also Spring Boot on the same datasource and would each run Flyway on boot by Spring's default. A repo-wide grep for 'spring.flyway', 'migrate on startup', 'init.?container', 'init.?job', 'baseline-on-migrate' returns ZERO hits across docs/ and PRD.md. No artifact disables Flyway on the worker/CronJob or gates migration. The race (multi-replica ALB-fronted API + worker + CronJob all booting concurrently against one schema-history lock) is real and undocumented.
verified_findings.finding: Three Spring Boot workloads (wc-api, wc-sync-worker, CronJob) connect to the same RDS PostgreSQL, yet no artifact assigns a Flyway migration owner or gating. Spring Boot runs Flyway on startup by default, so multiple workloads will race on the schema-history lock at deploy time; losers can fail readiness or crash-loop — a non-deterministic deploy failure with no documented owner.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In the finalized §14 name exactly one migration owner. Recommended for a one-week build: a dedicated pre-deploy Kubernetes Job (or Helm/Argo pre-deploy hook) that runs `flyway migrate` BEFORE the API/worker Deployments and CronJob roll. Set `spring.flyway.enabled=false` on wc-sync-worker and the CronJob so only the migration job touches the schema. State the hard deploy-ordering rule: worker/CronJob wait for migration completion (ordered GitHub Actions deploy or readiness on schema version).

verified_findings.title: CronJob is left as 'job/API' — never resolved to a 3rd image, an API mode, or an HTTP call
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §10 line 265 ('EKS CronJob invokes generation job/API'); §14 line 374 ('API and worker are separate container images.') and line 375 ('Worker and CronJob use Secrets Manager-injected config.'); DECISIONS.md line 55 ('Separate API and worker images', fallback 'One image with profiles only if build pipeline scope must shrink') and ADR-001 line 67 names the CronJob as a runtime but not its image; USER_FLOWS.md line 23 ('Kubernetes CronJob invokes the Spring Boot plan generation job/API'). The two-image decision plus the 'job/API' phrasing leave three unreconciled readings: third image, wc-api one-shot mode, or HTTP call to an internal endpoint. No artifact commits to one.
verified_findings.finding: The plan-shell generation CronJob's runtime identity is unresolved: third container image, a launch mode of the wc-api image, or a pod that POSTs to an internal API endpoint. Each choice changes the CI image matrix, the CronJob pod's IAM/secret scope, and whether an authenticated internal endpoint is needed. Task generation cannot proceed without picking one.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14/§10 pick the wc-api image launched in a one-shot generation mode (Spring profile or `--app.job=generate-plan-shells`), consistent with the 'separate API and worker images' decision and its 'one image with profiles' fallback. State explicitly: no third ECR image; CronJob = wc-api image batch entrypoint; reads DB secret only (not SNS/Graph). If instead an internal API call is chosen, document the auth for that internal call.

verified_findings.title: Cross-origin CORS between wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} and api.wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} is never specified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 lines 366-367 define two distinct origins (frontend `wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}` on S3/CloudFront, API `api.wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}` on ALB); §7 lines 155-172 define many PATCH/POST/DELETE mutation endpoints; §8 lines 190-191 and THREAT_MODEL.md line 13 define an Authorization-header + `X-Demo-Employee-Id` auth model. A repo-wide grep for 'cors|cross-origin|allow-origin|allowed origin' across docs/ and PRD.md returns ZERO hits. Browser CORS preflight on every non-simple cross-origin mutation is real; with no CORS policy the deployed app's mutations will fail in the browser, directly threatening REQ-E-006 (REQUIREMENTS.md line 174, demo proves AWS deployment through custom frontend/API domains).
verified_findings.finding: Frontend (wc.) and API (api.wc.) are different origins, so browsers enforce CORS preflight on all mutation calls carrying Authorization/demo headers. No artifact specifies allowed origins, methods, headers (Authorization, X-Demo-Employee-Id), credentials mode, or enforcement layer. Without it the deployed demo's mutations break even with a healthy API.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a CORS subsection to §14 (or §8): enforce CORS in Spring Security/MVC on wc-api with allowed-origin exactly `https://wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}` (plus `http://localhost:<vite-port>` for dev), methods GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS, allowed headers Authorization and the demo identity header, allowCredentials per the bearer-header transport. State ALB/CloudFront pass through and Spring owns CORS. Add a deployed smoke check that a cross-origin preflight + mutation succeeds.

verified_findings.title: Secrets injection mechanism (Secrets Store CSI Driver vs env/External Secrets) left unchosen
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed as deferred. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 line 375 ('Worker and CronJob use Secrets Manager-injected config') gives no mechanism. RESEARCH.md R-007 line 174 names 'the AWS Secrets and Configuration Provider for the Secrets Store CSI Driver' but line 189 explicitly defers: 'Exact EKS secret injection mechanism can be finalized in implementation.' The cited REQ-S-004 'env vars vs CSI file-mount' contradiction is OVERSTATED: REQUIREMENTS.md line 91 REQ-S-004 acceptance signal is 'Config uses environment variables and UI shows safe failure messages only' — its intent is no-hardcoding/rotatable, and both CSI and env approaches satisfy 'not baked into images' (REQ-S-010 line 97). So it is reconcilable, not a hard conflict. But the mechanism itself is genuinely unchosen and that materially changes the Terraform/k8s manifests, IRSA trust policy, and how Spring reads config — a real blocker for manifest task generation.
verified_findings.finding: The Secrets Manager injection mechanism (Secrets Store CSI Driver + ASCP, External Secrets Operator, or in-app SDK fetch) is researched but explicitly deferred. The choice changes the Terraform/k8s manifests, IRSA trust policy, and Spring config source (file vs env), blocking manifest task generation.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14 pick the Secrets Store CSI Driver + ASCP (the mechanism RESEARCH already cites) and state how Spring reads it (e.g. `spring.config.import=optional:file:/mnt/secrets/...` or an env-export init step). Note REQ-S-004's 'environment variables' wording is an intent signal, not a mandate, so a CSI file mount still satisfies it. Specify which secrets (DB, Auth0, Graph, DEMO flags) each workload mounts.

verified_findings.title: No per-workload IAM/IRSA mapping for SNS publish, SQS consume, and Secrets Manager read
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. THREAT_MODEL.md line 19 asserts 'least-privilege IAM' and 'EKS IAM' as the control for the EKS->Secrets Manager boundary but names no mechanism. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 line 371 lists 'IAM' among Terraform resources with no IRSA/pod-identity detail; §10 line 253 gives wc-api the 'SNS publisher' while §4 line 62 / §12 give the worker SQS consumption — distinct permission sets never separated. A repo-wide grep for 'irsa|pod identity|service account|iam policy' returns only the generic THREAT_MODEL mention; RESEARCH R-007 line 180 links the ASCP+IRSA doc URL but the body never specifies per-workload role bindings. Without an explicit SA->role mapping the default is a single broad node-group role granting every pod every permission, contradicting the asserted least-privilege control and weakening RISK-016/008 mitigations.
verified_findings.finding: The architecture asserts least-privilege IAM but never binds AWS permissions to specific EKS workloads via IRSA or Pod Identity. wc-api needs sns:Publish + secrets; wc-sync-worker needs sqs:Receive/Delete + the Graph secret (NOT sns:Publish); the CronJob needs only the DB secret. The likely implementation fallback — one broad node-group role — contradicts the claimed control.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add an IAM/IRSA table to §14: one IAM role per ServiceAccount per workload. wc-api SA -> sns:Publish on the lifecycle topic + secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on api/db/auth0/graph secrets; wc-sync-worker SA -> sqs:ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage/GetQueueAttributes on the sync queue + DLQ + GetSecretValue on the graph secret only; CronJob SA -> GetSecretValue on the DB secret only. Bind via IRSA (OIDC) or EKS Pod Identity; state which. Frame as the realization of the THREAT_MODEL least-privilege control.

verified_findings.title: SNS->SQS wiring details (subscription type, raw delivery, FIFO vs standard, redrive numbers) not stated
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed and correctly scoped low. verified_findings.finding: The concrete SNS->SQS subscription shape is unspecified: standard vs FIFO, raw message delivery, the SNS filter policy (so only Outlook-relevant lifecycle events enqueue), DLQ maxReceiveCount, and visibility timeout vs Graph call latency. verified_findings.title: Local dev has no defined SNS/SQS transport, so worker + Outlook E2E cannot run locally or in CI
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 lists ONLY 'Docker Compose for PostgreSQL and full-stack local services' / 'Demo Auth0 and Graph adapters enabled by local env' / 'Frontend/API/worker can run locally against Compose database' (lines 388-392) — no queue technology of any kind. A full-corpus grep for localstack/elasticmq/'in-process'/'local sns'/'local sqs'/stub/'embedded sqs' returns NOTHING addressing local transport. The only 'in-process' hits are ADR-003's DEPLOYED fallback ('If queue setup becomes a delivery blocker, process sync from the durable sync record in-process and document the variance', DECISIONS.md line 107) and §19's rejected alternative (ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md line 468) — neither defines local/CI transport. Meanwhile §4 step 5, §12 flow steps 3-5, REQ-I-009 ('SNS lifecycle fanout and SQS subscription delivery to a separate EKS worker'), and DECISIONS ADR-003 make SNS->SQS the SOLE API->worker path. REQ-T-016 ('Full Cypress/Cucumber suite runs against local CI/test services') plus the §16 locked 'Outlook warning/retry path' feature file and REQ-T-009 ('Integration tests cover Outlook sync success/failure/manual retry') require a job to actually flow API->queue->worker->sync-record locally. OPEN_QUESTIONS.md line 38 resolved 'How are Outlook sync jobs processed?' as the AWS path but says nothing local. CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF.md gap-audit item 10 ('CI/CD and local dev: ...Docker Compose, Testcontainers, GitHub Actions') flags this dimension as something the finalizer must resolve — it is not yet resolved.
verified_findings.finding: The architecture makes SNS->SQS->separate-worker the only transport between API and wc-sync-worker, but §15 never says how the worker receives jobs on a developer laptop or in the local CI E2E job. No LocalStack, no ElasticMQ, no in-process/demo queue adapter is specified, and the ADR-003 'in-process' fallback is scoped to a DEPLOYED-mode AWS-blocked deviation, not local/CI. As written the locked §16 'Outlook warning/retry' Cypress/Cucumber scenario (REQ-T-016) and the REQ-T-009 sync integration tests cannot exercise the API->queue->worker->sync-record->UI loop locally. Severity is 'important' rather than 'critical' for a one-week build because the sync record is the durable outbox: the API commits the sync record and the failure/retry UI state can be driven directly from sync-record state even if the worker hop is stubbed, so the demo and most acceptance signals degrade rather than hard-fail — but the locked end-to-end test still needs a defined local transport.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In final ARCHITECTURE.md §15, explicitly choose and document the local/CI queue strategy and state which is canonical for (a) developer Compose, (b) the CI local E2E job, and (c) deployed AWS. Recommended for one week: a profile-switched messaging adapter where the 'local/demo' profile, after the API commits the sync record (the durable outbox), invokes the worker consume logic in-process (or runs a LocalStack SNS+SQS container in docker-compose) so the same worker code path is exercised. Note that because the sync record is the durable outbox and manual retry republishes from the record (§12), the local adapter only needs to deliver the pointer payload, not reimplement SNS fanout semantics.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §15 (Local Development And Test Runtime); cross-refs §4 step 5, §12 Outlook Sync, §16 Testing (REQ-T-009, REQ-T-016, REQ-I-009)

verified_findings.title: CI-to-AWS authentication (OIDC vs. static keys) and the EKS/ECR deploy identity are undefined
verified_findings.verification_evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 CI/CD bullets (lines 377-384) stop at the verb level: 'Build/push API and worker images to ECR', 'Deploy EKS manifests', 'Build Vite frontend and sync to S3', 'Invalidate CloudFront as needed' — no auth mechanism. REQ-O-007 (REQUIREMENTS.md line 132) says the pipeline 'deploys EKS workloads, and syncs S3/CloudFront assets' but is silent on credentials. A corpus grep for oidc/configure-aws/'deploy role'/'assume role'/'access key'/'access entry'/update-kubeconfig/'web identity' returns NOTHING. HOWEVER, the boundary IS acknowledged: THREAT_MODEL.md line 21 names 'GitHub Actions -> AWS | Build artifacts, images, deploy credentials | GitHub, AWS IAM/ECR/EKS/S3 | CI secrets/IAM, quality gates | Supply-chain/deploy mistakes | GitHub Actions gates, ECR images, Terraform plan/apply discipline', and RISK-016 (RISKS.md line 27) plus REQ-S-010 (Secrets Manager, no hardcoded secrets) establish the no-long-lived-secrets posture the CI auth must honor. So the trust boundary and the security posture exist; only the concrete CI auth MECHANISM (OIDC federation + least-privilege deploy role + EKS access entry + kubeconfig) is missing.
verified_findings.finding: The GitHub Actions -> AWS trust boundary is named in THREAT_MODEL.md and the no-hardcoded-secrets posture is locked (REQ-S-010, RISK-016), but no artifact specifies HOW the pipeline authenticates: there is no mention of GitHub OIDC federation, a least-privilege CI deploy IAM role and its scope, or how the runner authenticates kubectl/helm to EKS (aws eks update-kubeconfig + EKS access entry / aws-auth). This is 'partial' rather than a clean confirmed_gap because the boundary and security constraints are documented; it is still 'important' because without the mechanism the deploy stages are non-executable and the implicit default of long-lived AWS keys in GitHub secrets would contradict the project's own Secrets-Manager posture.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'CI/CD identity' subsection to §14: use GitHub Actions OIDC federation (aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials with an OIDC trust) to assume one least-privilege CI deploy IAM role (ECR push, S3 sync, CloudFront invalidation, EKS describe + access for kubectl), provisioned by the same Terraform. Explicitly forbid long-lived AWS keys in GitHub secrets to stay consistent with REQ-S-010/RISK-016. Document the kubeconfig step (aws eks update-kubeconfig) and that the CI role is mapped via an EKS access entry / aws-auth entry. Acceptable one-week fallback to state: manual operator deploy with local creds, but OIDC is the documented target.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §14 (AWS Deployment / CI/CD); cross-ref THREAT_MODEL GitHub Actions->AWS boundary, REQ-S-010, RISK-016

verified_findings.title: Flyway migration execution is unspecified in the deploy pipeline and unsafe with two images on one RDS
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Flyway is locked (CONSTRAINTS.md line 35 'Flyway migrations'; DATA_MODEL.md line 11 'Migration tool: Flyway'; REQ-D-001 'Flyway schema covers all core entities'). But ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 CI/CD (lines 377-384) jumps from 'Build/push API and worker images to ECR' straight to 'Deploy EKS manifests' with NO migration step; §10 'Backend Service Architecture' (lines 239-267) and §6 (lines 113-135) describe schema/conventions but never say WHEN or WHERE Flyway runs. A corpus grep for 'on boot'/'on-boot'/migrate/baseline against the draft and DATA_MODEL.md surfaces only schema-baseline language, never migration EXECUTION ownership. The race risk is real and grounded: REQ-O-014 (REQUIREMENTS.md line 139) 'API and sync worker build as separate container images' + DECISIONS line 55 'Separate API and worker images', both sharing the single RDS (REQ-D-001), means Spring Boot's default on-boot Flyway could have the API ReplicaSet AND the worker (and multi-replica API pods) race to migrate the same database on rollout. Seed paths (REQ-D-004 RCDO seed, REQ-D-005 demo seed, REQ-D-008 optional 2,000-record perf seed) are likewise not tied to any migration/seed step in any environment.
verified_findings.finding: Neither §14 CI/CD nor §10/§6 defines when or where Flyway migrations run against RDS, or whether they run on app boot vs. as a pre-deploy CI step vs. a dedicated K8s Job/initContainer. With separate API and worker images sharing one RDS, default Spring Boot on-boot migration creates a real concurrent-migration race on rollout. The RCDO/demo/perf seed execution point is also unbound. Genuine gap; 'important' for a one-week build because a rollout migration race or unseeded environment directly threatens the deployed demo (REQ-E-006) and the local/CI test data the locked suites depend on.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14/§10, name the migration owner and ordering: run Flyway as a dedicated pre-deploy step — a Kubernetes Job / Helm pre-install,pre-upgrade hook gated before API/worker rollout, or a CI step against RDS before applying manifests — and disable on-boot migration on at least the worker so a single owner migrates (note Flyway's own migration lock makes concurrent attempts safe, but a single owner is cleaner). State where RCDO/demo seed runs (Flyway repeatable/seed migration or a one-shot seed Job) and that the 2,000-record perf seed (REQ-D-008) is a separate opt-in path, not part of normal deploy.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §14 (CI/CD) and §10 (Backend Service Architecture); cross-ref REQ-D-001/004/005/008, REQ-O-014

verified_findings.title: Terraform remote state backend, locking, and apply ownership (CI vs. manual) are unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Terraform is locked IaC (DECISIONS ADR-010 line 223; REQ-O-006 'Infrastructure is managed with Terraform'). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 'Infrastructure' (lines 369-375) lists provisioned resources and §14 'CI/CD' (lines 377-384) lists app build/deploy stages but NEVER mentions a Terraform state backend, state encryption, or who runs 'terraform apply'. A corpus grep for 'state backend'/tfstate/dynamodb/'state lock'/'remote state'/'terraform apply'/'plan-on'/'apply-on' surfaces only RISK-011 and OQ-002, both of which reference 'before Terraform apply' as a timing phrase for region checks — neither defines state backend or apply ownership. The draft's CI/CD bullet list omits Terraform entirely, leaving ambiguous whether apply is in-pipeline or operator-run.
verified_findings.finding: No artifact defines the Terraform state backend (S3 + DynamoDB lock is the AWS norm), state encryption, or whether 'terraform apply' is CI-driven or operator-run. Default local-only state on an assessment laptop is fragile (no locking, easy to lose) and a CI-driven apply re-raises the OIDC/credential question from the ci-aws-auth finding. Correctly scoped as nice-to-have for a one-week build — a documented manual/local apply is acceptable — but the choice must be stated so deploys are reproducible.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add to §14: declare an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB state locking and SSE; OR, if accepting a one-week simplification, explicitly document local state with a committed/exported plan and the manual-apply operator step. Reconcile the CI/CD bullet list with whether 'terraform apply' is in-pipeline or operator-run; if in-pipeline, it shares the OIDC CI role from the ci-aws-auth finding and should run plan-on-PR / apply-on-main.

verified_findings.title: CI prerequisites for Testcontainers (Docker-in-CI) and ECR image tag/versioning strategy are unstated
verified_findings.verification_evidence: (1) ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 (lines 394-397) 'Testcontainers PostgreSQL for Java integration tests. No H2 fallback'; REQ-T-017 confirms 'Java integration tests start PostgreSQL containers instead of H2'. A corpus grep for 'docker daemon'/'docker-in'/dind/runner/'github-hosted'/ubuntu-latest returns NOTHING — the Docker-daemon-on-runner prerequisite is never stated. (2) §14 (line 380) 'Build/push API and worker images to ECR' and (line 381) 'Deploy EKS manifests' with no image tag/version scheme; a corpus grep for tag/sha/':latest'/versioning/kustomize/helm/rollback finds no image tagging convention anywhere. Both are genuinely absent.
verified_findings.finding: Two pipeline mechanics are assumed but unstated: (1) Testcontainers requires a Docker daemon available to the GitHub Actions runner (GitHub-hosted ubuntu runners provide it), the local-dev cousin of the same Compose Docker dependency — never noted as a CI prerequisite; (2) no ECR image tag/versioning scheme (git SHA vs. latest) is defined, which the 'Deploy EKS manifests' step needs to reference the exact image just built and to enable rollback. Neither is contract-breaking, but both will block a clean pipeline run if left implicit. Correctly scoped as nice-to-have.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14/§16 note that CI runners must expose a Docker daemon for Testcontainers (GitHub-hosted ubuntu runners do) and that integration tests run on that stage. Define an image tag convention (immutable git-SHA tag pushed to ECR, optionally also a moving env tag) and that the EKS deploy step pins the SHA tag it just built via kustomize/Helm image override, enabling deterministic deploy and rollback.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §14 (CI/CD) and §16 (Testing And Quality Gates); cross-ref REQ-T-017, REQ-O-014

verified_findings.title: Heatmap drill-down endpoint has no pagination/bound, can violate the 2000-record discipline
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed at face value: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 165 `GET /api/manager/heatmap/{cellId}/drilldown` carries no page/size, while line 163 command-center has `?weekStart=&page=&size=`. §11 line 293 `Drill-down: Supporting Outcomes and commitments`. PRD.md:160 confirms drill-down = 'Supporting Outcomes and linked commitments'. REQ-NF-002 (REQUIREMENTS.md:105) and CONSTRAINTS.md:178 require team views to paginate and not load all records into the browser. BUT the unboundedness is overstated. A drilldown cell is structurally `(one manager_heatmap_cell row) = one manager x one direct report x one week x one Defining Objective` per the unique key `(manager_employee_id, employee_id, week_start_date, defining_objective_id)` (DATA_MODEL.md:326). The commitments under one such cell are one report's commitments for one week mapping under one of 3 Defining Objectives (REQ-D-004) — a handful of rows even at synthetic scale, since the 2,000 records are spread across many manager/report/week/DO combinations, not concentrated in a single cell. REQ-NF-002's 'up to 2,000 records' is explicitly a TEAM-VIEW (command-center list) concern, which is exactly the surface that DOES carry page/size. So this is not a genuine unbounded-list risk for MVP; it is an undocumented structural bound, not a missing one.
verified_findings.finding: The drilldown endpoint omits Pageable params, but the result is structurally bounded to a single (manager x report x week x Defining Objective) cell's commitments — a small set at any realistic scale given the 3-DO RCDO shape (REQ-D-004) and the per-cell unique key (DATA_MODEL.md:326). The real gap is documentation: the architecture never states this bound, so a downstream task generator could mistake it for an open unbounded list. The 200ms/no-load-all discipline (REQ-NF-002/003) is targeted at the command-center list, which is already paginated.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §11 or §7, add one sentence: the drilldown returns commitments for a single heatmap cell (one report x one week x one Defining Objective), which is structurally bounded and intentionally not paginated for MVP. No Pageable needed. This converts an apparent gap into a stated intentional bound for the finalizer/MVP_TASKS.

verified_findings.title: Comments retrieval is an unbounded full nested tree with no pagination or depth cap
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed at face value: §7 line 170 `GET /api/comments?targetType=&targetId=` has no page/size; §13 lines 349-350 'Full nested threads. Materialized path with parent comment and depth'; DATA_MODEL.md:224 `path varchar(2048)`, line 225 `depth integer`, index `(target_type, target_id, path)` at line 231 — no cap on node count or depth. DECISIONS.md line 48 locks 'Full nested comment threads using materialized path' (fallback: one-level threads if UI scope must be cut). ASSUMPTIONS.md has no comment-volume assumption. HOWEVER the severity is overstated. The finding's claim that comments 'bloat GET /plans/current and manager flows' is NOT supported by the artifacts: §7 lists `GET /api/comments` as a SEPARATE endpoint keyed by target, and §9 RTK Query (line 231) lists 'comments' as its own API slice/tag — comments are fetched on demand per target, not inlined into the plan-retrieval DTO. §7 line 175 lists DTO fields (IDs, labels, state, timestamps, RCDO breadcrumbs, risk badges, allowed actions) — comments are NOT among them. So comments do not load on the 200ms plan-retrieval common path. Crucially, §20 line 492 ALREADY defers this: 'Deep nested-comment UI rendering, while preserving schema' is under 'Trim first', meaning MVP need not render deep trees.
verified_findings.finding: The comments read path has no pagination or depth cap and is the one genuinely unbounded result-size read in §7. But it is on a dedicated, target-scoped, separately-tagged endpoint (not inlined into plan/manager retrieval per §9 RTK Query slices and §7 DTO fields), so it does not threaten the 200ms common path. §20 already lists deep nested-comment rendering under 'Trim first.' The residual gap is that no server-side node/depth cap or assumed max-comments-per-target is documented, so an unbounded tree could in principle be requested.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §13, add one MVP sentence: document an assumed-small comment volume per target and a server-side max returned node count + depth cap (since §20 already trims deep nested rendering). This consciously bounds the only unbounded read without adding pagination scope to a one-week build.

verified_findings.title: Command-center filters required by REQ-F-023 are absent from both the endpoint contract and the projection columns
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed and correctly characterized. REQ-F-023 (REQUIREMENTS.md:34) and PRD.md:151 require dashboard filters by person, plan state, review state, Defining Objective, Supporting Outcome, priority, work type, AND alignment status (8 dimensions). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §7 line 163 declares ONLY `?weekStart=&page=&size=` for command-center — zero filter params. DATA_MODEL.md manager_plan_summary columns (lines 278-294) hold manager_employee_id, employee_id, plan_state, review_status, review_due_at, is_review_overdue, and aggregate counts (planned/unplanned/misaligned/needs_review/blocked/carry_forward/unresolved_dispute) — but NO priority, work_type, supporting_outcome_id, or alignment_status columns. So 4 of the 8 REQ-F-023 filters cannot be served from manager_plan_summary; serving them would force joins/scans back to weekly_commitment, which directly tensions REQ-NF-003 (REQUIREMENTS.md:106 'avoid N+1... backend-owned and indexed') and CONSTRAINTS.md:179. weekly_commitment DOES index `(supporting_outcome_id)` and `(alignment_status)` (DATA_MODEL.md:159,161) but NOT priority or work_type. The heatmap is keyed by defining_objective_id (DATA_MODEL.md:312) so the DO filter has a home, but SO/priority/work-type/alignment-status filters have no declared serving path on either projection. This is a genuine API-contract + read-model design gap, not covered anywhere.
verified_findings.finding: REQ-F-023's 8-dimension dashboard filter set is unserviceable from the declared design: §7 command-center declares no filter params, and manager_plan_summary lacks columns for priority, work_type, supporting_outcome, and alignment_status. Four filters (SO, priority, work type, alignment status) have no documented indexed serving path, and weekly_commitment only indexes supporting_outcome_id and alignment_status (not priority/work_type), so naive filtering risks the N+1/scan path REQ-NF-003 forbids.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §7, expand command-center query params to cover REQ-F-023, and in §6/§11 decide per-filter how each is served: person/plan-state/review-state on manager_plan_summary directly; DO via the heatmap cell grain; SO/priority/work-type/alignment-status via an explicitly indexed commitment-level filtered query (add the missing priority/work_type indexes to weekly_commitment, or add those filter dimensions to the projection). Name the index path for each so no N+1 emerges, OR explicitly scope command-center filters to projection-held columns and document that finer filters live on the heatmap/drilldown surface.

verified_findings.title: The 200ms plan-retrieval target has no defined measurement method (percentile, scope, warm/cold, tool)
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. The 200ms target is stated identically and method-free across every layer: OG_PRD.md:25 'API response times under 200ms for plan retrieval'; PRD.md:391 'Plan retrieval API response time under 200ms for common paths'; REQUIREMENTS.md:104 REQ-NF-001 'should target under 200ms' with acceptance 'Performance test or documented benchmark covers common retrieval path'; REQ-T-012 (line 158) 'Evidence included in test results'; CONSTRAINTS.md:176 'Common plan retrieval API response target: under 200ms'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §16 line 430 'Plan retrieval under 200ms common path.' None of these define percentile (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end vs server-side vs DB-only, warm vs cold JVM, single-client vs concurrent, which endpoints constitute 'plan retrieval', or the measurement tool. EVALUATION_CRITERIA.md:42 only requires 'paginated/aggregated backend queries' (query strategy credibility), not a pinned latency method. §17 (Observability) provides Actuator/CloudWatch but never wires a timer to the 200ms gate. The gate is genuinely unfalsifiable as written.
verified_findings.finding: The 200ms target appears in 6 artifacts with no measurement method: no percentile, no scope (e2e/server/DB), no warm/cold definition, no concurrency model, no enumeration of which endpoints count as 'plan retrieval', and no tool. REQ-T-012 only asks for 'evidence' and EVALUATION_CRITERIA only asks that the query strategy be 'credible', so the implementer cannot know what passes. This is a real, unambiguous gap.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16, pin a one-week-appropriate method: e.g. 'p95 server-side latency (controller-in to response-out via Micrometer/Actuator timer or a JUnit+Testcontainers timing harness) for GET /plans/current and GET /api/manager/command-center, warm JVM, single-client, against the 2,000-record synthetic seed', and name the artifact where the numbers land. This turns REQ-T-012 'evidence' into a defined pass/fail. Severity 'important' is right given EVALUATION_CRITERIA.md:18 explicitly judges on testability.

verified_findings.title: GET /api/manager/heatmap has no row/result bound; fine for demo grain but undocumented at synthetic scale
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed and correctly self-scoped as low-risk. §7 line 164 heatmap endpoint has no page/size (it carries `?weekStart=&definingObjectiveId=&supportingOutcomeId=`). §11 lines 290-291 rows=direct reports, columns=Defining Objectives. CONSTRAINTS.md:116 and ASM-009 (ASSUMPTIONS.md:20) lock the demo to 1 manager with 5-8 reports; REQ-D-004 (REQUIREMENTS.md:72) locks 3 Defining Objectives. So a heatmap is at most ~5-8 reports x 3 DOs = ~24 cells per week — trivially bounded and well within 200ms. manager_heatmap_cell indexes `(manager_employee_id, week_start_date)` (DATA_MODEL.md:327) which serves this read directly. The finding itself acknowledges this is low-risk; the only genuine deficiency is that the structural bound (direct-report count x active DOs for one week) is never stated. This is a documentation nicety, not a performance defect.
verified_findings.finding: The heatmap endpoint omits pagination, but is structurally bounded to direct-report-count x active-Defining-Objectives for the requested week — ~24 cells at the locked demo grain (1 manager, 5-8 reports, 3 DOs). It is served by the `(manager_employee_id, week_start_date)` index. The only gap is that this intentional bound is not documented, so it could be mistaken for an unbounded-list omission.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §11 or §7, add one sentence stating the heatmap result is structurally bounded by direct-report count x active Defining Objectives for the week (small per ASM-009), so omitting pagination is intentional. No code change for MVP.

verified_findings.title: 2,000-record synthetic seed path is named but its shape and how it maps onto the projection tables is unspecified
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed as a real but minor underspecification. REQ-D-008 (REQUIREMENTS.md:76) says 'up to 2,000 team-view records'; CONSTRAINTS.md:117 'separate optional synthetic 2,000-record dataset path supports performance tests' and line 178 'Team views should handle up to 2,000 records'; ASM-009 (ASSUMPTIONS.md:20) 'separate synthetic performance seed for 2,000-record tests'; §16 line 432 'Heatmap/projection query checks using synthetic 2,000-record dataset'; DECISIONS.md:36 'optional 2,000-record perf seed'. NONE of these define what the 2,000 records ARE (plans? commitments? manager_plan_summary rows?) or their manager/week distribution. This matters because projection indexes are manager+week scoped (manager_plan_summary index `(manager_employee_id, week_start_date, plan_state)` DATA_MODEL.md:299; manager_heatmap_cell index `(manager_employee_id, week_start_date)` DATA_MODEL.md:327): whether 2,000 records concentrate under one manager/week (the worst case the pagination is FOR) or spread thin determines whether the indexed paginated read is genuinely exercised. The phrase 'team-view records' (REQ-D-008) weakly implies manager_plan_summary rows, but distribution is never pinned. Genuinely unspecified, though low-risk for a one-week build since the perf gate itself (per finding 200ms-no-measurement-method) is the higher-order issue.
verified_findings.finding: The 2,000-record synthetic seed — the only fixture the 200ms/no-N+1/pagination claims validate against — is named in 5 artifacts but its record grain and manager/week distribution are never defined. 'team-view records' (REQ-D-008) hints at manager_plan_summary rows but does not pin distribution. Since the projection indexes are manager+week scoped, a thin spread would fail to exercise the paginated indexed read that the worst-case (one heavily-loaded manager/week) is designed for.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16 (or a note in §11), define the seed shape: e.g. 'N managers x M reports across W weeks producing ~2,000 manager_plan_summary rows and ~Z manager_heatmap_cell rows, with at least one manager/week loaded to the pagination ceiling so the indexed paginated read is exercised against the realistic worst case.' Best fixed jointly with the 200ms method finding.

verified_findings.title: CORS is never specified as a security control on the cross-origin API boundary
verified_findings.verification_evidence: grep for 'cors|cross-origin|allow.*origin|allowed.?origin' across docs/planning/ and PRD.md returns ZERO hits (run confirmed). The split is real: CONSTRAINTS.md:158-159 'Frontend custom domain: wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}. API custom domain: api.wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN}'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 lines 366-367 same. THREAT_MODEL.md line 12 'Browser -> WC API ... Controls: Auth0 JWT validation or env-gated demo auth; DTO validation; server authz' — CORS omitted. §18 critical-controls list (lines 452-460) and §8 (lines 188-208) never mention CORS. So this is a genuine, fully-confirmed gap: every browser->API call crosses an origin boundary and no allow-list is specified anywhere.
verified_findings.finding: The deployed system is a hard cross-origin split: frontend at wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} (CloudFront) calls the API at api.wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} (ALB). Every authenticated browser->API call crosses an origin boundary and requires a CORS policy, yet CORS appears nowhere in the planning corpus. Because auth is a bearer JWT in a header (not a cookie), the data-exfiltration risk of a permissive policy is lower than for cookie auth, but a missing/over-broad CORS config is the single most likely reason the deployed SPA silently fails its first API call — a buildability/deploy-correctness risk on a one-week timebox. The demo X-Demo-Employee-Id header path makes 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' undesirable but it is gated by DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED so the production blast radius is bounded.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §18 (and the Browser->WC API row of THREAT_MODEL.md) specify an explicit env-driven CORS allow-list: allowedOrigins defaults to https://wc.${ROOT_DOMAIN} plus http://localhost:5173 for local dev; enumerate allowedMethods/allowedHeaders; no wildcard origin; allowCredentials=false since auth is bearer-token. Note demo mode must NOT relax CORS. Add a deployed smoke check (extend RISKS.md:53 deployment-smoke list) that a preflight from the real frontend origin succeeds and a foreign origin is rejected.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §18 critical controls (and §8 / §14); THREAT_MODEL.md Browser->WC API boundary row

verified_findings.title: JWT validation is named but issuer/audience/JWKS/signing-algorithm specifics are not pinned
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Binding artifacts stop at the headline: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §8 line 190 'Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server validates Auth0 JWT issuer/audience'; §18 line 454 'Auth0 issuer/audience validation in real mode'; THREAT_MODEL.md line 14 'issuer/audience validation, configurable claims' and line 81 test 'JWT with wrong issuer/audience rejected'. RESEARCH.md R-002 lines 57-58 notes Spring 'validates JWTs using issuer URI and can validate audience. JWK Set URI can be configured directly when needed' — so JWKS is acknowledged as available but NOT bound into the draft. grep confirms zero hits for rs256/alg=none/signature/jwk outside that one RESEARCH.md line. So audience IS named (the claim that audience is omitted is wrong); but signing-algorithm pinning (RS256-only, reject alg=none/HS256-with-public-key) and explicit JWKS signature verification are genuinely unbound. Mitigates from 'fully missing' to underspecified because issuer+audience and a wrong-issuer/audience test already exist.
verified_findings.finding: ADR-equivalent REQ-S-007/REQ-S-009 require real Auth0 JWT validation and the draft binds issuer AND audience plus a wrong-issuer/audience rejection test (THREAT_MODEL.md:81) — so the strongest version of this finding (audience omitted) is overstated. What is genuinely unpinned: (1) signature verification against Auth0 JWKS rather than just claim-reading, (2) RS256-only with alg=none/symmetric-algorithm rejection, (3) exp/nbf and clock-skew handling. Standard Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server defaults already do JWKS signature verification and reject alg=none when configured via issuer-uri, which softens real-world likelihood, but on a one-week build with a 'configurable claim mapper' an implementer can wire a decode-only path. Worth pinning, not critical.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §8 add: validate signature against Auth0 JWKS via issuer-uri auto-discovery (or explicit jwk-set-uri), require RS256 and reject alg=none/symmetric algorithms, mandatory issuer AND audience validation (audience = the WC API identifier), enforce exp/nbf with bounded clock skew. Add a security test for a correctly-signed token with the WRONG audience being rejected, alongside the existing wrong-issuer test at THREAT_MODEL.md:81.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §8 Authorization/Authentication; §18 critical controls; THREAT_MODEL.md Auth0->WC API boundary

verified_findings.title: No rate limiting / abuse control on the public API, and no DoS control for the demo-header path
verified_findings.verification_evidence: grep for 'rate.?limit|throttl|waf|brute' across docs/planning/ and PRD.md returns ZERO hits (run confirmed). THREAT_MODEL.md DoS section (lines 60-66) covers only heatmap/DB query load (read-model tables, indexes, pagination) and Outlook retry loops. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §14 line 373 'API ingress uses AWS Load Balancer Controller / ALB' names no WAF/throttle. The threat model presents itself as a full STRIDE pass (lines 23-74) yet the DoS branch is silent on edge/app rate limiting. Genuine omission, correctly self-rated nice-to-have for a one-week assessment.
verified_findings.finding: The API is internet-facing on a custom domain behind an ALB with no WAF or throttling, and the STRIDE DoS branch only addresses query load and retry loops. For a one-week assessment build this is at/over the overbuild line — implementing rate limiting is correctly out of scope — but because THREAT_MODEL.md frames itself as a complete STRIDE pass, the absence should be a conscious documented deferral rather than a silent hole.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a one-line deferral under §18 and the THREAT_MODEL.md DoS section: 'Edge rate limiting / WAF is a deliberately deferred control — PA edge owns it in production; the assessment relies on bearer-token auth plus ALB defaults.' If any control is desired the lowest-cost option is an AWS WAF rate-based rule on the ALB. Documenting the deferral is sufficient; do not build it.

verified_findings.title: Nested-comment body and markdown rendering are an unenumerated XSS surface
verified_findings.verification_evidence: The XSS surface IS covered generically: RISK-015 (RISKS.md:26) 'User-entered text creates XSS or unsafe rendering ... frontend escaping ... Fallback: Block rich markdown in MVP'; REQ-S-005 (REQUIREMENTS.md:92) explicitly lists 'comments' in the validation/escaping acceptance signal; §18 line 460 'Server-side validation for HTML/script text'; THREAT_MODEL.md:83 test 'Script/HTML content is escaped or safely rendered'. So escaping is required and markdown-blocking is already the named fallback — the claim that the surface is unaddressed is overstated. What is genuinely thin: the cross-actor (manager-comment-rendered-in-IC-browser) stored-XSS path is not named, and §13 line 354 leaves markdown as a possible add ('unless time allows') WITHOUT pinning that markdown-if-added must go through a sanitizing allow-list renderer. comment.body is 'text not null' (DATA_MODEL.md:226) across 4 target types (line 220) with authorization inheriting target visibility (line 238 / §13 line 352), confirming the cross-trust-boundary render is real.
verified_findings.finding: Comment body is the highest-value stored-XSS surface (free text, nested, rendered across the IC<->manager trust boundary) but the corpus already mandates escaping (REQ-S-005, RISK-015, THREAT_MODEL.md:83) and already names 'block rich markdown' as the fallback — so this is not an unaddressed gap. The residual real risk is two-fold and worth pinning: (1) the cross-actor render path is not explicitly called out, and (2) §13:354 invites markdown 'if time allows' without binding the rule that markdown MUST use a sanitizing allow-list renderer (no raw HTML / no dangerouslySetInnerHTML), which is the one place the generic 'escape on render' control could be silently defeated.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §13/§18 add: classify comment.body, managerNote, ic_response, and outcome_note as stored-XSS surfaces rendered across the IC<->manager trust boundary; render as plain text via React default escaping (never dangerouslySetInnerHTML); IF markdown is enabled it MUST go through a sanitizing allow-list renderer (no raw HTML) and markdown is the trim point — drop markdown before sanitization. Add a test where a manager-authored script/img-onerror comment renders inert in the IC's browser and vice versa.

verified_findings.title: CloudWatch log content is not constrained — sensitive review/dispute data and PII can leak into logs
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Existing controls cover only SECRETS, not sensitive BUSINESS data: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §17 line 446 'Audit metadata should avoid secrets and sensitive token details'; THREAT_MODEL.md:54-55 only 'Graph/Auth0 secrets leak through logs/UI -> no token logging'; RISK-016 (RISKS.md:27) is secrets-only. Meanwhile CloudWatch is the sink for API/worker/CronJob (§17:440, REQ-O-009). PRD lines 403-404 'Alignment disputes and manager notes are sensitive review data and require audit logging'; CONSTRAINTS.md:188 same. PRD:423 (REQ-O-001) requires logs 'include enough context to reconstruct a reported issue without exposing sensitive secrets' — note: it says secrets, NOT business PII. So nothing instructs the implementer to keep dispute notes / comment bodies / employee email out of free-text CloudWatch logs, where they escape the domain authorization scope. Genuine info-disclosure gap distinct from the secrets gap.
verified_findings.finding: The corpus carefully forbids secrets/tokens in logs but never constrains logging of sensitive business data (manager notes, dispute rationale, comment bodies, employee email). These are designated sensitive review data (PRD:403, CONSTRAINTS.md:188) yet REQ-O-001's mandate to log 'enough context to reconstruct an issue' (PRD:423) plus free-text logging could push them into CloudWatch, where they are no longer access-scoped by the domain authorization service. The 'reconstruct a reported issue' phrasing actively pulls toward over-logging. Important because it is a distinct, plausible disclosure path on a tight build, and the fix is cheap (logging discipline, not new infra).
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Extend §17 and the THREAT_MODEL.md Information Disclosure row: CloudWatch logs must use structured logging of IDs and state transitions, NOT free-text manager notes, ic_response, comment bodies, dispute rationale, or employee email/PII; request/response body logging off by default; constrain log levels on sensitive paths. Reuse the same 'safe metadata' discipline already required for audit_event (§17:446, DATA_MODEL.md audit_event.metadata_json).

verified_findings.title: Demo-header-rejection and other security events are absent from the audit_event action list
verified_findings.verification_evidence: The §17:445 audit catalog enumerates 'plan lock, reconciliation start/close, carry-forward, review, dispute open/respond/resolve, sync success/failure, and authorization denial' — it includes authorization denial but NOT demo-header-rejection or JWT-validation-failure. THREAT_MODEL.md:27-28 mitigates the backdoor by rejecting the header and lines 73-74 (EoP) say only 'smoke checks should verify expected auth mode' — no runtime audit/alert. RISK-008 (RISKS.md:19) treats the backdoor as Critical. audit_event.action is free-text varchar(100) (DATA_MODEL.md:338) so adding actions is zero-schema-cost. Confirmed: the two most security-sensitive runtime events (RISK-008 backdoor probe; spoofing detection via wrong issuer/audience) produce no audit trail. Correctly self-rated nice-to-have for a one-week build.
verified_findings.finding: The audit catalog includes 'authorization denial' but omits DEMO_AUTH_HEADER_REJECTED (header presented while DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED=false — the RISK-008 production-backdoor signal) and JWT_VALIDATION_FAILED (the spoofing-detection signal from THREAT_MODEL.md:81). So an operator who accidentally ships with demo mode on, or an attacker probing for it, leaves no evidence. Low cost to close (audit_event.action is free-text), low likelihood in a single-week assessment, hence nice-to-have.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add two security actions to the §17 audit catalog: DEMO_AUTH_HEADER_REJECTED and JWT_VALIDATION_FAILED, both written to audit_event with safe metadata (no token). This makes the RISK-008 backdoor and the spoofing threat observable at runtime, complementing the deploy-time smoke check already noted at THREAT_MODEL.md:74.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §17 Audit; §18; THREAT_MODEL.md Elevation Of Privilege / Spoofing

verified_findings.title: OVERDUE supersession is documented but the security/audit angle of the derived status is thin
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Supersession is well documented and self-consistent in the planning corpus: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §3 line 47 'overdue is derived'; DATA_MODEL.md:189 'isOverdue = now > review_due_at and status = NOT_REVIEWED'; manager_review.status check omits OVERDUE (DATA_MODEL.md:176); REQ-F-012 (REQUIREMENTS.md:23) 'OVERDUE is derived ... not stored'; DECISIONS.md:15. Note PRD lines 233-235 DO draw OVERDUE as a review state ('NOT_REVIEWED -> OVERDUE -> REVIEWED') — so the draft intentionally diverges from the PRD diagram and that divergence is captured in REQ-F-012/DECISIONS, NOT a silent contract break (the finding correctly concedes this). Real but minor.
verified_findings.finding: The OVERDUE-derived decision is documented and consistent; the only residual is observability plumbing: PRD:415 / REQ-O-001 list 'review overdue' as a required logged lifecycle signal, but a derived (never-stored) status has no transition event to emit, so it is unclear how REQ-O-001's overdue signal is satisfied without contradicting REQ-F-012. verified_findings.title: Comment model targets MANAGER_REVIEW and ALIGNMENT_DISPUTE, which the PRD never asks for
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed. Every requirement/brief/PRD reference to comments scopes them to plans/commitments ONLY, never review or dispute records: PRD.md L101 'Comment on commitments/plans', L456 'Manager can comment on plans/commitments'; PRODUCT_BRIEF.md L200 'Manager comments on a plan or commitment'; REQ-F-014 (REQUIREMENTS.md L25) 'Manager can comment on direct-report locked plans/commitments'; REQ-D-014 acceptance signal (L82) '...and target scope for plan/commitment discussion.' Also note the dispute already carries structured manager_note (DATA_MODEL L202) + ic_response (L203) fields, so a comment thread on a dispute is duplicative. Keep the materialized-path column shape and target_type as VARCHAR so the constraint can be widened later, and add one sentence documenting review/dispute-targeted comments as deferred. verified_findings.title: Full nested materialized-path comment threads are gold-plating vs the thesis, even with UI deferred
verified_findings.verification_evidence: The factual claims check out. OG_PRD.md mentions no comment threading. PRD.md L101/L456 say only 'comment'. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §19 L470: 'One-level comments: rejected after user chose full nested comments.' DECISIONS.md L48 Comments row: 'Full nested comment threads using materialized path | Locked ... Fallback: One-level threads if UI scope must be cut.' RISK-012 (RISKS.md L23) is severity Medium with fallback 'One-level/flat UI rendering while preserving schema.' DATA_MODEL.md L213-237 confirms path varchar(2048), depth, and the (target_type,target_id,path) index. The trim order (RISKS L38, DRAFT §20 L492) correctly defers nested UI while preserving schema. BUT this is explicitly a user-chosen locked decision (DECISIONS L48, DRAFT §19 L470, both 'confirmed by user'), so it must be surfaced to the human, not silently downgraded. verified_findings.finding: The materialized-path nested-comment schema and its write-path logic (path computation, depth maintenance, ordered retrieval) advance none of the five evaluation standards or locked invariants, and threading is absent from both PRD and OG_PRD. verified_findings.title: Two synchronous projection tables fan out duplicate risk-count writes on every commitment mutation
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed accurate on the facts. manager_plan_summary (DATA_MODEL L272-300) and manager_heatmap_cell (L302-328) both carry the same seven count columns: planned_count, unplanned_count, misaligned_count, needs_review_count, blocked_count, carry_forward_count, unresolved_dispute_count — at per-report/week vs per-report/week/objective grain. Both update synchronously on the same write set: DATA_MODEL L353-354 'Projection updates occur synchronously with affected domain writes. Writes that affect summary/heatmap include commitment create/update/delete, plan lock, reconciliation start/close, manager review, dispute open/respond/resolve, and carry-forward creation.' Mirrored in DRAFT §11 L276-281 and §10 L260. ADR-006 (DECISIONS L141-160) names the exact relief valve: fallback L158-160 'If projection implementation becomes too heavy, keep manager_heatmap_cell and compute manager_plan_summary live.' RISK-003 fallback (RISKS L14) 'Compute affected summary live if projection fails.' HOWEVER the claim that the draft's trim order never lists collapsing to one projection is TRUE: DRAFT §20 L491 only says 'Projection rebuild niceties' and RISKS Trim Order L37 says 'Projection rebuild niceties, while keeping synchronous projections' — neither surfaces the ADR-006 live-summary collapse as a trim path. verified_findings.finding: manager_plan_summary and manager_heatmap_cell duplicate seven risk-count columns and both update synchronously inside every affected service transaction. plan_summary counts are derivable by aggregating heatmap cells across objectives, so the dual synchronous write fan-out is partially redundant. ADR-006 already specifies the right relief valve (keep heatmap, compute summary live) but neither §20 nor the RISKS Trim Order surfaces it as a concrete trim path — they only mention vague 'projection rebuild niceties.'
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Keep both tables, but add an explicit trim step to §20 / RISKS Trim Order mirroring ADR-006's fallback: 'If synchronous dual-projection write fan-out causes latency or build cost, keep manager_heatmap_cell as the source projection and compute manager_plan_summary roll-ups live by aggregating cells.' verified_findings.title: Trim order correctly protects thesis + AWS + security; minor framing tightenable

verified_findings.title: Overdue/SLA derivation has no injectable time source, making the core derived-state invariant non-deterministically testable
verified_findings.verification_evidence: The mechanism (injectable java.time.Clock / fixed clock) is genuinely absent: grep across docs/planning + PRD.md for 'clock|time source|time inject|frozen clock' returns zero hits. DATA_MODEL.md:189 defines the derived field as `isOverdue = now > review_due_at and status = 'NOT_REVIEWED'` with a wall-clock `now`. HOWEVER the testability INTENT is covered: ASSUMPTIONS.md ASM-008 says the SLA design 'Keeps due-date logic deterministic and testable' with 'Unit tests around Friday/weekend cases', and REQUIREMENTS REQ-T-004 requires 'reviewDueAt and overdue signal cases pass', and REQ-F-013 requires the REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES-not-overdue branch. So the corpus commits to deterministic SLA tests but never specifies HOW time is held fixed. This is a real underspecification of mechanism, not a missing requirement. Severity lowered from critical to important: for a one-week build the implementer can trivially inject a Clock, and the requirement to test it deterministically already exists (REQ-T-004, ASM-008); the gap is that the binding architecture doesn't mandate the seam.
verified_findings.finding: DATA_MODEL.md:189 computes the overdue invariant against a wall-clock `now`, and §16/REQ-T-004/ASM-008 all require overdue + reviewDueAt + Friday/weekend cases to be tested deterministically, but no artifact specifies the time-abstraction mechanism that makes those assertions deterministic. Without a named injectable clock, REQ-T-004's overdue branches and REQ-F-013's REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES-satisfies-SLA branch are asserted via flaky date math or sleeps. ASM-008 already promises 'deterministic and testable' SLA, so the architecture should make good on that promise mechanically.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16 (and §10 service boundaries) mandate an injectable java.time.Clock bean used by the reviewDueAt calculator and the overdue read-path derivation. Add explicit fixed-Clock unit-test requirements: (a) NOT_REVIEWED + now>due => overdue true; (b) NOT_REVIEWED + now<=due => overdue false; (c) REVIEWED_WITH_DISPUTES + now>due => NOT overdue (REQ-F-013); (d) REVIEWED => never overdue; plus the weekday-only reviewDueAt calculation (REQ-O-003, ASM-008) across a weekend with a fixed Clock.
