verified_findings.title: Weekly plan-shell generation CronJob and its idempotency guard are absent from the test plan
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed that ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §16 contains no test for generation/shells/idempotency: the backend unit list (line 408) is 'lifecycle, SLA, baseline immutability, disputes, sync state', the integration list (409) is 'JPA/Flyway, authorization, projections, sync records', and the E2E list (421-426) has no generation scenario. The idempotency guard exists in design (§10:266 'DB unique constraint on employee/week provides final idempotency guard'; DATA_MODEL weekly_plan unique (employee_id, week_start_date); REQ-F-001 acceptance 'Rerunning generation for the same employee/week does not create duplicates'; REQ-I-002 'Plan generation creates no Graph sync records'). So the BEHAVIOR is specified with an acceptance signal, but the §16 TEST PLAN omits a test that exercises it. This is a real test-plan gap, NOT a missing requirement (REQ-F-001/REQ-I-002 already define the acceptance signals). Severity lowered from critical to important: the acceptance signal already exists and the unique constraint is the actual enforcement; the missing piece is binding the test to §16.
verified_findings.finding: REQ-F-001's acceptance signal ('rerunning generation does not create duplicates') and REQ-I-002 ('generated shells create no Graph sync records') are load-bearing for a retried/concurrent EKS CronJob, but §16 never lists a generation/idempotency test. The unique constraint (DATA_MODEL weekly_plan) is the real guard, yet no §16 test proves re-invocation is a no-op or that shells produce zero sync records.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Add a §16 integration-test requirement (Testcontainers PostgreSQL) for the generation entrypoint: (1) one DRAFT shell per active employee for the target Monday-Sunday week in org timezone (REQ-F-002); (2) re-invoking generation for the same week does not duplicate or violate the unique constraint; (3) duplicate/concurrent invocation surfaces the DB unique constraint, not a duplicate row; (4) generated shells create zero outlook_calendar_sync_record rows (REQ-I-002). Test via the invoked generation job/API, not k8s scheduling.

verified_findings.title: No specified test seam for the async SNS/SQS path and the sync worker; Testcontainers is scoped to PostgreSQL only
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed genuinely missing. §15 (396-398) names only 'Testcontainers PostgreSQL ... No H2 fallback for persistence behavior' with no queue equivalent; grep for 'localstack|elasticmq|embedded sqs|embedded sns' across docs/planning + PRD returns zero hits. The worker is a separate deployable (§4 wc-sync-worker; ADR-009 separate image) with a 6-state machine (§12:303-310 PENDING_PUBLISH->QUEUED->SYNCING->SYNCED/FAILED/RETRY_REQUESTED) and a pointer-payload contract (REQ-I-014, §12:323-330). §16 integration list says 'sync records' and E2E says 'Outlook warning/retry path', but neither describes how the SNS->SQS->worker boundary or the worker handler is exercised below deployed E2E. THREAT_MODEL 'SQS -> Sync Worker' boundary lists 'state transitions' as the control but no test seam. This is a real gap: the worker's state machine and pointer-payload consumption have no specified local/CI test seam.
verified_findings.finding: §15 scopes Testcontainers to PostgreSQL only and no artifact specifies how the SNS-publish -> SQS-deliver -> worker-consume path or the worker message handler is tested deterministically (no LocalStack/ElasticMQ, no worker-handler unit seam). The worker's 6-state machine (§12) and pointer-payload load-from-DB contract (REQ-I-014) are therefore only exercisable in non-deterministic deployed E2E, which is outside the local CI gate (§15:399-402).
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §15/§16 specify the async test strategy: (a) worker message-handler unit/integration tests that invoke the consumer directly with a pointer payload against Testcontainers PostgreSQL plus a demo Graph adapter, asserting the §12 state transitions and graphEventId capture independent of live SQS; (b) optionally one LocalStack/ElasticMQ Testcontainer end-to-end publish->consume contract test; (c) state that real SNS/SQS delivery is validated only in the deployed smoke suite. Make explicit that the worker is unit-testable by injecting the queue message.

verified_findings.title: JaCoCo 80% threshold does not specify per-module scope across api + worker + shared Gradle modules
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed the scope is unspecified: §16:410 says only 'JaCoCo minimum 80%' (singular, unscoped); grep for 'per-module|aggregate coverage|each module' returns zero hits. The multi-module layout that creates the ambiguity is real: ADR-009 (DECISIONS:198-213) 'Gradle multi-module for Java modules shared by the API and worker', REQ-O-016 'Gradle modules separate shared code, API app, and sync worker app', §21:515. So the finding correctly identifies that 'JaCoCo 80%' could be satisfied as an aggregate that masks a weak worker/shared module. HOWEVER this is a refinement of an already-locked gate (ADR-005 / REQ-T-013), affecting only HOW the threshold is computed, not whether coverage exists. For a one-week build the default Gradle JaCoCo verification is per-subproject anyway. Severity lowered from important to nice-to-have: real but a precision/wording improvement, not a correctness or coverage gap.
verified_findings.finding: §16's 'JaCoCo minimum 80%' is singular and unscoped while ADR-009/REQ-O-016 establish separate api, worker, and shared Gradle modules. An aggregate 80% could let a well-tested API mask an under-tested wc-sync-worker or shared module — exactly where the highest-risk logic (sync state machine, idempotency, SLA/Clock helpers) lives.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16 state that JaCoCo verification runs per Gradle module with an 80% minimum on each of wc-api, wc-sync-worker, and the shared module (pick line or instruction coverage), not as a single aggregate. List any justified per-module exclusions (generated DTOs, config) explicitly.

verified_findings.title: Synchronous projection consistency, drift, and the rebuild job/CLI lack a specified test approach
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed §16 is generic on this: integration list (409) says 'projections' only and performance (432) says 'Heatmap/projection query checks'. The behaviors are precisely specified elsewhere: ADR-006 (DECISIONS:141-160) 'rows update synchronously in the same service transaction'; DATA_MODEL 'Projection Update Rules':351-356 enumerates every trigger (commitment CRUD, plan lock, reconciliation start/close, manager review, dispute open/respond/resolve, carry-forward) plus 'internal rebuild job/CLI can truncate/recompute ... from source tables'; §11:276-285 repeats the triggers; REQ-D-012/D-013; RISK-003 (High, projection drift) and RISK-014 (High, wrong risk badges). RISKS Risk Validation:50 lists 'Unit tests: ... projection aggregation' and :51 'Integration tests: ... projection rows'. REQ-T-008 only asserts 'counts/risk badges match seeded data' — which does NOT exercise transactional rollback coupling or drift-vs-rebuild equivalence. So: triggers and rebuild ARE specified, but no test requires (a) same-transaction rollback coupling or (c) rebuild==incremental equivalence. Genuine but partial gap; severity important because RISK-003/RISK-014 are both High.
verified_findings.finding: ADR-006/DATA_MODEL require projections to update inside the same service transaction as the triggering write, and REQ-D-013/§11 require a rebuild job/CLI, but §16 only says 'projections' generically and REQ-T-008 only checks counts match seeded data. No test requires: (a) the projection write rolls back with the enclosing domain transaction on failure; (b) every §11 trigger produces the expected projection delta; (c) rebuilt projections equal incrementally-maintained ones (drift detection per RISK-003); (d) heatmap risk badges match seeded source cases (RISK-014).
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §16 require Testcontainers integration tests that: (1) assert each §11 / DATA_MODEL 'Projection Update Rules' trigger produces the expected delta; (2) assert the projection write rolls back when the enclosing domain transaction fails (transactional coupling); (3) run a sequence of mutations then the rebuild job/CLI and assert rebuilt == incremental (RISK-003); (4) assert heatmap risk badges match seeded source cases (RISK-014).

verified_findings.title: Idempotent retry (no duplicate Graph event, reuse graphEventId) is not specified as a concrete, deterministic assertion
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Confirmed the assertion MECHANISM is unspecified. REQ-T-009 acceptance is 'retry is idempotent' and RISKS Risk Validation:51 lists 'Integration tests: ... sync record retry' and THREAT_MODEL:85 lists 'Sync retry does not create duplicate events' — so the test INTENT is well-covered across the corpus, more than the finding implies. BUT the deterministic seam is genuinely under-specified: §12:332-336 describes demo success/failure adapters as 'deterministic' but does NOT say the demo adapter exposes observable create-vs-update / call-count behavior an assertion can check; grep for 'call count|create.vs.update|observable' returns zero hits. §12:342 says graphEventId 'is used to update ... rather than create duplicates where possible' (soft 'where possible'). The unique index (DATA_MODEL outlook_calendar_sync_record (owner, related_type, related_id, event_kind)) is the real structural guard. So the test is REQUIRED (REQ-T-009, THREAT_MODEL) but HOW idempotency is asserted (the adapter seam) is missing. Partial, important (RISK-005 High).
verified_findings.finding: REQ-T-009 ('retry is idempotent'), THREAT_MODEL ('sync retry does not create duplicate events'), and RISK-005 (High) all require proving manual retry (FAILED->RETRY_REQUESTED, §12:343) does not duplicate Graph events and reuses graphEventId. The demo adapter is the natural deterministic seam (§12:332-336) but §12 never says it exposes create-vs-update / call-count behavior a test can assert, and §12:342 hedges idempotency with 'where possible'. Without that observable seam the 'retry is idempotent' assertion has no defined mechanism.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §12/§16 designate the demo Graph adapter as the deterministic test seam and require it to expose observable create-vs-update behavior (or call counts). Add an integration test: first sync sets graphEventId; manual retry transitions FAILED->RETRY_REQUESTED, re-processes the SAME sync record, and asserts the adapter performed an UPDATE on the existing graphEventId (or a single create + zero duplicate rows given the unique (owner, related_type, related_id, event_kind) index), with retry_count incrementing (DATA_MODEL outlook_calendar_sync_record).

verified_findings.title: The five BDD feature files under-cover the documented acceptance/demo signals, and the dispute scenario omits the IC-response leg
verified_findings.verification_evidence: Mixed and partly overstated on framing. §16 E2E list (421-426) has 5 items, and 'Manager review/dispute/resolve' (424) does collapse the REQ-T-011 loop ('manager review/flag/IC response/manager resolve') so the distinct IC-respond-cannot-resolve leg (REQ-F-017, EVALUATION_CRITERIA Demo Signal 'IC responds: IC can revise/rationalize but cannot resolve') is not visibly its own scenario. HOWEVER claim (1) is partly covered: §16:422 already lists 'IC draft/lock/reconcile/carry-forward' as an E2E feature — so the lock path and carry-forward ARE in the E2E set; the SPECIFIC missing scenario is the lock-REJECTION-on-unlinked-commitment moment (REQ-E-001 / EVALUATION_CRITERIA Disqualifying gap 'A planned commitment can lock without a Supporting Outcome' / Demo Signal 'IC tries to lock unlinked work'), which is genuinely not called out in §16 and is the headline strategy-enforcement proof. Claim (4) carry-forward-not-rewriting-baseline (REQ-E-005) is a deeper assertion than the generic 'carry-forward' E2E entry. So this is a real but partial gap: the rejection path and the discrete IC-response leg are the genuine omissions; some sub-claims are already in §16. Severity important given REQ-T-015 locked Cypress/Cucumber primacy + Disqualifying gap status.
verified_findings.finding: Cypress/Cucumber is the primary, locked acceptance suite (ADR-005, REQ-T-015). §16's 5 E2E features omit/collapse the most contract-critical moments: (1) no scenario for lock-REJECTION-on-unlinked-commitment (REQ-E-001), which EVALUATION_CRITERIA names a Disqualifying gap and a required Demo Success Signal; (2) the 'Manager review/dispute/resolve' entry collapses REQ-T-011's loop and does not surface the discrete IC-response-but-cannot-resolve leg (REQ-F-017); (3) carry-forward appears as a happy-path E2E entry but not as the REQ-E-005 assertion that it leaves the locked baseline unchanged. The single most important contract behavior (enforced linkage at lock) is not a visible BDD scenario.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: Expand §16's BDD set, mapped 1:1 to requirement IDs: (a) 'IC cannot lock a plan with an unlinked planned commitment' (REQ-E-001) AND the success-lock path; (b) the full dispute loop as discrete steps including the IC-response leg with an explicit assertion that the IC cannot resolve (REQ-F-017); (c) unplanned-work + carry-forward leaving the locked baseline unchanged (REQ-E-005).

verified_findings.title: RDS PostgreSQL 16.4 is no longer a currently available minor version (latest 16.x is 16.14)
verified_findings.verification_evidence: External fact CONFIRMED: AWS 'what's new' May 2026 (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/amazon-rds-postgresql/) lists currently supported 16.x as 16.14 (and Feb 2026 listed 16.13); 16.4 is absent from current minors and AWS published a 'minor versions deprecating on May 31, 2026' notice. RDS only lets you CREATE on currently-available minors, so a fresh instance on exactly 16.4 will be rejected. The corpus PARTIALLY covers this but is factually wrong in one place and stale in others: RESEARCH.md R-004 (lines 103-104) asserts 'Amazon RDS PostgreSQL release notes list PostgreSQL 16.4 variants. Newer 16.x versions exist, but the PRD pin should remain the architecture target unless region availability blocks it' — this is incorrect; the blocker is not region availability, it is that 16.4 is no longer creatable in ANY region. RISK-011 (RISKS.md line 22) DOES anticipate the problem with a fallback ('Use closest supported 16.x only if evaluator accepts deviation') but mis-rates likelihood as 'Low' and frames it as region-specific. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md hard-pins '16.4' at §1 line 13, §14 line 371; DECISIONS.md line 23 and ADR-001 line 67, and CONSTRAINTS.md lines 32/155 pin it as 'locked requirement from PRD.' Critically, PRD.md itself pins '16.4' (lines 317, 349), so this is a grader-specified version, not an architecture invention.
verified_findings.finding: The '16.4' pin is no longer creatable on RDS as of June 2026 (current 16.x minors are 16.13/16.14), so a literal Terraform apply on engine_version='16.4' will fail. The corpus is split: RISK-011 has a fallback but underrates it as low-likelihood/region-specific, and RESEARCH.md R-004 actively records the wrong reason (it claims 16.4 is listed and only region availability could block it). Because the PRD pins 16.4 as a hard requirement, this is a real but contained issue: the intent is 'PostgreSQL major 16', and the safe move is to pin major 16 on the latest available 16.x minor.
verified_findings.proposed_fix: In §14 and the §1/§4 prose, change the DB target from frozen '16.4' to 'PostgreSQL major version 16 on the latest available RDS 16.x minor at provision time (>=16.13)'. Make the minor a Terraform variable with auto_minor_version_upgrade=true. Correct RESEARCH.md R-004 to record that 16.4 is no longer creatable on RDS (not a region issue). Re-rate RISK-011 likelihood up and reword from region-specific to 'minor deprecated'. Add a one-line note that this satisfies the PRD's 'PostgreSQL 16' intent and flag for human sign-off since the PRD literally says 16.4.
verified_findings.arch_anchor: §14 (also §1, §4); RESEARCH.md R-004; RISKS.md RISK-011; DECISIONS.md ADR-001

verified_findings.title: Spring Boot 3.3 reached end of OSS support on 2025-06-30 — no free security patches
verified_findings.verification_evidence: External fact CONFIRMED: Spring blog (https://spring.io/blog/2025/06/19/spring-boot-3-3-13-available-now/) marks 3.3.13 (2025-06-19) as the final OSS release; OSS support for 3.3.x ended 2025-06-30; only paid commercial support continues. The corpus does NOT cover the lifecycle status anywhere: RESEARCH.md R-002 (lines 51-72) covers only Spring Security JWT config, never the Spring Boot version EOL. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §4 line 61 pins 'Spring Boot 3.3'. DECISIONS.md/CONSTRAINTS.md treat it only as a 'locked requirement from PRD.'
